meta.description: 桌游本体 — 统一定义游戏中的静态结构概念与流程时序概念。不定义具体游戏规则。
meta.convention:
每个概念的 constraints.required 表示：若另一个概念继承或引用此概念，则必须提供这些字段的值。程序递归收集父链上的所有 required 约束和顶层字段。

类型约定（type field convention）：字段的 type 值分为三类——(1) 概念引用：type 为已有概念的 id（如 player、zone、object、cost、content、information_visibility），表示该字段的值是对该概念实例的引用；(2) 泛引用：type 为 concept_ref，表示引用目标不限于单一概念，程序或 LLM 需根据上下文确定具体目标类型；(3) 原始类型：直接使用类型名——string、integer、boolean、any、map<string, any>、enum。enum 类型附带内联的 enum 数组枚举合法值。字段可空性由约束语境表达（constraints.optional 或 default: null），type 中不写「| null」后缀；字段 key 本身为 <concept_id> 格式时不再声明 type（key 即类型）。

交叉引用约定（cross-reference convention）：所有 definition 和 field description 文本中，引用其他概念时使用 <concept_id> 占位符包裹概念 id。例如「指向游戏中一个具体的 <object> 实例（<player>、<zone>、<piece> 等，均为 <object> 的子类）」。LLM 读取时可据此识别交叉引用并沿 <concept_id> 查找对应概念的定义。

description.zh: 可被识别、引用或操作的实体或抽象概念。
description.en: An entity or abstract concept that can be identified, referenced, or operated upon.

description.zh: 唯一标识符。所有 <object> 实例必须通过此字段被识别和引用。由 <object> 自身定义，隐式赋予所有子类实例。
description.en: Unique identifier. All <object> instances must be identifiable and referenceable through this field. Defined by <object> itself, implicitly available to all subclass instances.

description.zh: 描述该对象固有特征的键值对集合。由游戏规则预定义，描述对象「是什么」而非「此刻怎样」。注意：attributes 对应的是 Property（属性），不是 State（状态）。
description.en: A map of key-value pairs describing the object's intrinsic characteristics. Predefined by game rules. Describes what the object 'is', not what it 'currently is' (which would be State).

description.zh: 直接参与游戏并能够做出决策的实体。<player> 是游戏中的能动主体——它发起 <action>、拥有 <object>、积累 Score、最终参与胜负判定。<player> 继承自 <object>。
description.en: An entity that directly participates in the game and is capable of making decisions. <player> is the active agent in the game — it initiates <action>s, owns <object>s, accumulates Score, and ultimately participates in victory determination. <player> extends <object>.

description.zh: 玩家名称，用于 UI 显示和 LLM 自然语言生成，不影响规则逻辑。
description.en: Player name for UI display and LLM natural language generation. Does not affect rule logic.

description.zh: 玩家在回合顺序中的位置（从 1 开始）。用于决定行动先后。若游戏采用其他顺序机制（如同时行动、竞标决定顺序），此字段可为空。
description.en: The player's position in turn order (1-based). Used to determine action sequence. May be empty if the game uses other ordering mechanisms (e.g. simultaneous action, bidding).

description.zh: 一种可被 <player> 拥有、计数、转移和消耗的价值概念。<resource> 继承自 <object>。其核心特征是可计量——玩家持有的是「3 个蓝宝石」而非「一个叫蓝宝石的物件」。同一类型的 <resource> 的所有个体完全等价、可互相替代。与 <marker> 的区别在于：resource 会被 action 的 <cost> 消耗或作为 <effect> 产出，而 marker 只用于指示状态。
description.en: A value concept that can be owned, counted, transferred, and spent by <player>s. <resource> extends <object>. Its defining feature is countability — a player holds '3 blue gems', not 'a thing called blue gem'. All units of the same <resource> type are completely equivalent and interchangeable. Unlike a <marker>, a resource is consumed by an action's <cost> or produced by an <effect>; a marker only indicates state.

description.zh: 此资源的计量单位。如宝石用「颗」、钱币用「枚」、木材用「根」。仅供 UI 和 LLM 生成自然语言时使用，不影响规则逻辑。
description.en: The unit of measurement for this resource. E.g., '颗' for gems, '枚' for coins. For UI and natural language generation only; does not affect rule logic.

description.zh: 此资源的外观描述。如「蓝色六边形宝石，表面有切割纹理」「金黄色圆形硬币，正面有五角星图案」。用于动画生成、UI 渲染和 AI 讲解时帮助玩家识别实物，不影响规则逻辑。
description.en: Visual description of this resource. E.g., 'blue hexagonal gem with cut texture', 'golden round coin with a star on the front'. Used for animation, UI rendering, and AI explanations to help players identify physical pieces. Does not affect rule logic.

description.zh: 用于表示此资源的那个看得见摸得着的小零件。如棕色八角柱代表食物。若为 null，说明此资源本身外观特征明显、玩家一看就知道是什么。
description.en: The tangible small piece used to represent this resource. E.g., a brown octagonal pillar represents food. If null, the resource is self-evidently identifiable.

description.zh: 一种特殊的 <resource>，代表玩家在游戏中获得的分数或胜利点数（victory points）。<score> 继承自 <resource>，核心特征是可被计数和增减，通常不用于支付费用或转移给其他玩家，而是用于胜负判定。典型例子包括璀璨宝石中的声望点数、文明演化中的分数。
description.en: A special <resource> representing a player's points or victory points. <score> extends <resource>. Its defining feature is that it is countable and can be increased or decreased; it is typically not spent as a cost or transferred to other players, but is used for victory determination. Typical examples include prestige points in Splendor and score points in Civolution.

description.zh: 一种游戏零件，携带 <effect> 并可改变游戏状态。<piece> 继承自 <object>。并非所有 piece 都由玩家持有——归游戏系统所有（<ownership> 为 null）的 piece 不可被玩家 <play>，而是作为游戏环境的一部分存在（如地图板块、遭遇牌库）。只有 <ownership> 归属于 <player> 的 piece 才可被该玩家 <play>——打出它、建造它、激活它，游戏状态会因此改变。<piece> 与 <component> 的本质区别：<piece> 携带 <effect>；<component> 没有 <effect>，只负责标记事实。<effect> 的静态形态是 <property>——「这张牌的费用是 3 蓝」「打出后获得 2 分」「每轮结束时获得 1 银币」都是 <effect> 的规格说明。某些 <piece>（如 <card>、<tile>）可以承载 <zone>——zone 的生命周期绑定在宿主 piece 上，宿主被移除时 zone 随之消失。一块物理 piece 可能印有多重逻辑身份——通过 <parts> 字段声明，如大陆板块上印有地形区域和建造点、发展卡上印有费用和折扣和声望分；各 part 拥有独立的 concept parent 和属性，规则引擎按各自身份分别查询。
description.en: A game component that carries <effect>s and can change game state. <piece> extends <object>. Not all pieces are owned by players — pieces owned by the game system (<ownership> is null) cannot be <play>ed by players; they exist as part of the game environment (e.g., map tiles, encounter decks). Only pieces whose <ownership> belongs to a <player> can be <play>ed by that player — playing, building, or activating it causes game state changes. The essential difference between <piece> and <component>: a <piece> carries <effect>s; a <component> has no <effect>s and only marks facts. <effect>s in static form are <property>s — 'this card costs 3 blue', 'gain 2 points when played', 'gain 1 silver at the end of each round' are all <effect> specifications. Some <piece>s (e.g., <card>, <tile>) can host <zone>s — the zone's lifecycle is bound to the host piece and disappears when the host is removed.

description.zh: 此物件的外观描述。必须包含 AI 向玩家解释规则时所需的关键视觉信息——信息标注在什么位置、图案和颜色长什么样。如「矩形卡牌，左上角白色数字为该牌的分数，中央下方为效果文本」「棕色六角形厚纸板片，正面中央印有白色城堡图案，无数字标注」。AI 回答「怎么看」类问题时主要依赖此字段。
description.en: Visual description of this piece. Must include key visual information needed for AI to explain rules to players — where information is printed, what patterns and colors look like. E.g., 'rectangular card, the white number in the top-left is the victory points, effect text is centered below', 'brown hexagonal tile with a white castle icon in the center, no numbers'. AI relies on this field when answering 'how do I see...' questions.

description.zh: 此 piece 物理载体上印有的逻辑组件列表。一块实体板/卡上可能印有多种身份独立的组件——如大陆板块上印有地形区域、营地、材料格、建造点，或发展卡上印有费用、折扣、声望点数。每个元素拥有独立的 concept parent 和自身属性（zone、effect、property 等），规则引擎按各自身份分别查询。用「拿刀裁开即独立 piece」来理解——物理合一、逻辑分立。
description.en: A list of logical components printed on this physical piece. One physical board/card may carry multiple independently identifiable components — e.g., a continent tile printed with terrain zones, encampments, material slots, and a building ground site; or a development card printed with cost, discount, and prestige points. Each element has its own concept parent and properties (zones, effects, etc.), queried independently by the rule engine. Think of it as 'cut them apart with a knife and each is an independent piece' — physically united, logically separate.

description.zh: 一种承载游戏状态的物理组件。<board> 继承自 <object>。与 <aid> 的本质区别：<aid> 是纯被动参考物——上面的信息只是画上去的，收起来也不影响游戏；<board> 则承载游戏状态——上面可以放置 <piece> 和 <component>、可以容纳 <zone>（zone 虽由规则定义，但 board 是它的物理宿主）、可以携带自身的 <content>（如玩家面板上印着的活动图标能力，不依赖任何外部 <piece> 即可使用）。与 <piece> 的本质区别：<piece> 可以被 <transfer>——打出、交换、弃掉、移动；<board> 不可被转移——它固定属于某个 <player> 或公共区域，整个游戏过程中不会易主。<board> 的子类包括 <public_board> 和 <player_board>。
description.en: A physical component that carries game state. <board> extends <object>. The essential difference from <aid>: an <aid> is a purely passive reference — the information on it is merely printed, and putting it away does not affect the game; a <board> carries game state — <piece>s and <component>s are placed on it, it can host <zone>s (zones are defined by rules, but the board is their physical host), and it can carry its own <content> (e.g., the activity icon ability printed on a player console, usable without any external <piece>). The essential difference from <piece>: a <piece> can be <transfer>red — played, exchanged, discarded, moved; a <board> cannot be transferred — it is fixed to a <player> or the public area and never changes hands during the game. Subclasses include <public_board> and <player_board>.

description.zh: 版图外观描述——形状、材质、尺寸和上面印有的内容。AI 向玩家介绍版图布局时的核心信息来源。
description.en: Visual description of this board — shape, material, size, and what is printed on it. Core information source when AI introduces board layout to players.

description.zh: 此版图上承载的 <zone>。每个 zone 至少包含 `position`（该 zone 在版图上的物理位置描述，如「左上角」「右半部」），可选包含 `description`（补充说明）。注意：zone 本身由规则独立定义——board 不「创造」zone，board 只是 zone 的物理宿主。客人问「某某东西放哪」时，系统通过此字段找到位置信息并给出精确回答。
description.en: The <zone>s hosted on this board. Each zone contains at minimum `position` (physical location description on the board, e.g., 'top-left corner', 'right half'), optionally `description` for additional notes. Note: zones are independently defined by rules — the board does not 'create' zones, it is merely their physical host. When a guest asks 'where do I put X', the system uses this field to find the position and give a precise answer.

description.zh: 此版图自身携带的效果或能力。不需要打出任何 <piece> 即可使用——这些能力直接印在版图上，由版图自身赋予玩家。例如 Civolution 玩家面板上的基础活动图标。数组中的每项描述一个独立的能力或效果。这些内容在版图进入游戏时自动生效，不依赖任何外部 <piece>。
description.en: Effects or abilities carried by this board itself. Usable without playing any <piece> — these abilities are directly printed on the board and granted to the player by the board itself. E.g., the basic activity icon on a Civolution player console. Each entry in the array describes one independent ability or effect. These contents take effect automatically when the board enters the game, independent of any external <piece>.

description.zh: 用于向 <player> 展示参考信息、辅助玩家识别和操作的游戏实体。<aid> 继承自 <object>。其核心特征是「不承载游戏状态」——它上面的信息只是画上去的，不因游戏进程而改变；它上面不放置 <piece> 或 <component>，也不容纳 <zone>。<aid> 是纯参考物：规则书被合上、玩家提示卡被收起来，游戏规则依然存在并生效。熟练玩家在脑中记住了所有规则后，完全可以不借助 <aid> 进行游戏。注意：如果一块板子上面可以放置棋子、需要翻面、会被放标记——它承载游戏状态，则它不是 <aid>，应归入 <board>。
description.en: A game entity used to present reference information to <player>s and assist in recognition and operation. <aid> extends <object>. Its defining trait is that it 'carries no game state' — the information on it is merely printed and does not change with gameplay; no <piece>s or <component>s are placed on it, and it hosts no <zone>s. An <aid> is a pure reference: close the rulebook, put away the player aid, and the game rules still exist and apply. A skilled player who has memorized all rules can play entirely without <aid>s. Note: if a board has pieces placed on it, needs to be flipped, or receives markers — it carries game state — then it is not an <aid> and should be categorized as a <board>.

description.zh: 辅助物外观描述——形状、材质、尺寸和上面印有的内容。AI 向玩家介绍版图布局和辅助工具时的核心信息来源。
description.en: Visual description of this aid — shape, material, size, and what is printed on it. Core information source when AI introduces board layout and helper tools to players.

description.zh: 此辅助物在视觉上对应哪些 <zone>。注意：Aid 不「包含」这些 zone，它只是把它们画在了上面——这种映射是单向的视觉关联。Zone 的存在和属性完全由规则定义，与 Aid 无关。
description.en: Which <zone>s this Aid visually corresponds to. Note: the Aid does not 'contain' these zones; it merely depicts them. This is a one-way visual association — Zones exist and have properties defined purely by rules, independent of any Aid.

description.zh: 桌游中最常见的小型物理零件。<component> 继承自 <object>。它代表盒子里那些看得见摸得着、但自身高度抽象的小零件——八角柱、圆片、方块、米宝等。一个 <component> 本身不决定自己代表什么；它与游戏概念的关联是外在的、可变的——同一个棕色八角柱，放在仓库里代表食物，放到重置轨上代表重置标记。<component> 本身不携带 <effect>，不能被 <play>——它不会因为被放置或移动而自己改变游戏状态；真正改变状态的是规则 <event>。
description.en: The most common small physical piece in board games. <component> extends <object>. It represents those tangible, highly abstract little parts in the box — octagonal pillars, discs, cubes, meeples, etc. A <component> itself does not determine what it represents; its association with game concepts is external and mutable. A <component> itself carries no <effect> and cannot be <play>ed — placing or moving it does not change game state by itself; the rules <event> does.

description.zh: 零件外观描述——形状、尺寸、颜色、材质。AI 向玩家解释实物识别时的核心信息。
description.en: Visual description of this component — shape, size, color, material. Core information for AI to help players identify physical pieces.

description.zh: 此零件代表什么逻辑概念。若一个零件是多用途的（红色方块既能计分又能标归属），此字段为空，含义由它当前所在的 <zone> 或使用上下文决定。
description.en: What logical concept this component represents. For multi-purpose components, leave empty — the meaning is determined by its current <zone> or usage context.

description.zh: 用于指示某个 <state> 或位置的概念。<marker> 继承自 <object>。它不被当作资源消耗，而是被放置、移动或移除来反映游戏规则中的状态变化。典型例子包括：阶段标记、天气标记、进程轨标记、计分标记、起始玩家标记等。
description.en: A concept used to indicate a <state> or position. <marker> extends <object>. It is not spent as a resource; instead it is placed, moved, or removed to reflect state changes defined by the rules. Typical examples include phase indicators, weather indicators, progress track markers, score markers, and starting player markers.

description.zh: 标记物外观描述——形状、尺寸、颜色、材质。
description.en: Visual description of this marker — shape, size, color, material.

description.zh: 此标记物代表的逻辑概念（如 State「起始玩家」、State「当前阶段」）。
description.en: The logical concept this marker represents (e.g., State 'starting player', State 'current phase').

description.zh: 用于表示此标记物的那个看得见摸得着的小零件。如蓝色圆片代表分轨标记。若为 null，说明此标记物本身外观特征明显、玩家一看就知道是什么。
description.en: The tangible small piece used to represent this marker. E.g., a blue disc represents a score track marker. If null, the marker is self-evidently identifiable.

description.zh: 用于标记谁是起始 <player> 的 <marker>。<starting_player_marker> 继承自 <marker>。它是许多桌游中的通用组件——持有此标记的 <player> 即为当前 <round> 的起始玩家。每 <round> 结束后，标记传递给下一位 <player>，对应的 <starting_player> 状态随之更新。
description.en: A <marker> used to mark who is the starting <player>. <starting_player_marker> extends <marker>. It is a common component in many board games — the <player> holding this marker is the starting player for the current <round>. After each <round>, the marker is passed to the next <player>, and the corresponding <starting_player> state is updated.

description.zh: 游戏中的抽象逻辑容器，表示一组 <object> 的空间归属关系。不依赖版图和实体，只由规则决定。<zone> 是抽象概念，子类包括 <reserve>、<discard_pile>、<player_zone>、<track> 等。
description.en: An abstract logical container in the game, representing the spatial belonging of a set of <object>s. Independent of board and physical components; defined solely by rules. <zone> is an abstract concept; subclasses include <reserve>, <discard_pile>, <player_zone>, <track>, etc.

description.zh: Zone 的唯一标识符。继承自 <object>，用于在游戏规则中精确引用特定 Zone 实例。
description.en: Unique identifier of the Zone. Inherited from <object>, used to precisely reference a specific Zone instance in game rules.

description.zh: 声明此 Zone 允许存放哪些类型的 <object>。程序校验 <transfer> 时以此过滤——若 what 的类型不在 contains 中，<transfer> 非法。空数组表示不限类型。
description.en: Declares what types of <object> this Zone allows. Programs check this when validating a <transfer> — if what's type is not in contains, the <transfer> is illegal. Empty array means any type is allowed.

description.zh: 此 Zone 的所有权归属。决定该 Zone 及其中的 <object> 属于哪个 <player>。null 表示公共区域，所有玩家均可访问。
description.en: Ownership of this Zone. Determines which <player> owns this Zone and its contents. null means public — all players can access.

description.zh: 此 Zone 的信息可见性级别。决定 Zone 中的内容可被哪些 <player> 观察——公开区全员可见，手牌区仅拥有者可见，牌堆区仅顶部部分可见等。
description.en: Information visibility level of this Zone. Determines which <player>s can observe its contents — public zones are visible to all, hand zones are owner-only, deck zones may be partially visible at the top, etc.

description.zh: 可容纳的对象数量上限。null 表示无上限。达到上限后，以此区域为目标的 Transfer 将被拒绝。
description.en: Maximum number of objects this zone can hold. null means unlimited. When full, Transfers targeting this zone are rejected.

description.zh: 某个时刻游戏世界中为真的断言。描述游戏实体「此刻怎样」，而非「是什么」。<state> 是运行时事实，随时可被 <effect> 改变。
description.en: A true assertion about the game world at a given moment. Describes what a game entity 'currently is', not what it 'is'. <state> is a runtime fact, changeable at any time by <effect>s.

description.zh: State 的唯一标识符。用于在规则中精确引用特定状态实例（如「Player A 的分数」「Card X 的横置状态」）。
description.en: Unique identifier of the State. Used to precisely reference a specific state instance in rules.

description.zh: 此 State 描述的实体——回答「谁此刻怎样」中的「谁」。指向一个具体的 <object> 实例（<player>、<zone>、<piece> 等）。
description.en: The entity this State describes — the 'who' in 'who is currently in what state'. Points to a concrete <object> instance.

description.zh: 状态值的类型约束。如 "integer"、"boolean"、"player"。程序修改状态时以此校验。
description.en: Type constraint for the state value. E.g., "integer", "boolean", "player". Programs validate state changes against this.

description.zh: 游戏开始时的初始值。用于 setup 和 reset。
description.en: Initial value when the game starts. Used for setup and reset.

description.zh: <object> 或 <zone> 固有的、由游戏规则预先定义的特征。描述游戏实体「是什么」「拥有什么能力」「具备什么特点」。默认不可变——在 <object> 进入游戏时即确定，仅在 <effect> 明确修改时才变化。<property> 是 <cost>、<content>、<effect>、<information_visibility> 的父概念。
description.en: An intrinsic characteristic of an <object> or <zone>, pre-defined by game rules. Describes what a game entity 'is', 'what abilities it has', 'what traits it possesses'. Immutable by default — set when the <object> enters the game, only changed by an explicit <effect>. <property> is the parent of <cost>, <content>, <effect>, <information_visibility>.

description.zh: Property 的唯一标识符。用于在规则中精确引用特定属性（如「Card X 的费用」「Zone Y 的可见性」）。
description.en: Unique identifier of the Property. Used to precisely reference a specific property in rules.

description.zh: 此 Property 附着于什么概念或实体——回答「谁拥有这个特征」。可指向本体概念（如 "card"，表示所有卡牌）或具体实例。
description.en: What concept or entity this Property attaches to — answers 'who has this characteristic'. Can point to an ontology concept or a specific instance.

description.zh: 属性值的类型约束。如 "integer"、"boolean"、"cost_map"、"effect_spec"。
description.en: Type constraint for the property value. E.g., "integer", "boolean", "cost_map", "effect_spec".

description.zh: 是否可被游戏效果修改。默认 false（静态）。若为 true，修改必须经由 Effect 触发，不可被玩家随意更改。
description.en: Whether this property can be modified by game effects. Default false (static). If true, modification must go through an Effect — players cannot arbitrarily change it.

description.zh: 对象被创建或进入游戏时的默认值。
description.en: Default value when the object is created or enters the game.

description.zh: 标识一个 <event> 是否为每位 <ontology::player> 各执行一次——程序化分发，不重视排他性和行动顺序（如 setup 中每位玩家各获得自己的组件）。domain 为事件类概念（<transfer>、<play>、<state_change> 等），任何事件都可挂载。若场景强调行动顺序（必须按座次依次操作、一次只能一人操作），应改用流程树的 <round> + <turn> 结构而非此属性。
description.en: Marks an <event> as executing once for each <ontology::player> — programmatic distribution, without emphasis on exclusivity or turn order (e.g., each player receiving their own components during setup). Domain is event concepts (<transfer>, <play>, <state_change>, etc.); any event may carry it. If strict turn order is required (players act one at a time in seating order), use the <round> + <turn> structure of the flow tree instead of this property.

description.zh: 通用替换工具：声明将 target 路径指向的任何对象替换为 with。**任何概念都可以选择持有 <ontology::replaces> 字段**（<trigger>、<effect>、<action>、<cost>、<content> 等）——持有方在 condition 成立时执行替换。被替换对象可以是任意可引用物——内容、作用目标、代价等。with 为 _skip 哨兵 = 使目标无效/取消。与 <substitution> 互补：substitution 声明「X 视为 Y」（身份借用），<replaces> 声明「用 Y 替换 X」（对象替换）。
description.en: A general replacement tool: declares that whatever object the target path points to is replaced by `with`. **Any concept may choose to carry an <ontology::replaces> field** (<trigger>, <effect>, <action>, <cost>, <content>, etc.) — the carrier performs the replacement when its condition holds. The replaced object can be any referenceable thing — content, target, cost, etc. with = the _skip sentinel nullifies/cancels the target. Complements <substitution>: substitution declares 'X counts as Y' (identity borrowing); <replaces> declares 'Y replaces X' (object replacement).

description.zh: 被替换对象的路径引用（"<概念>.<字段>.<子字段>" 形式）。
description.en: Path reference to the object being replaced (of the form "<concept>.<field>.<subfield>").

description.zh: 替换后的对象。_skip 哨兵 = 使目标无效/取消。
description.en: The replacement object. The _skip sentinel = nullify/cancel the target.

description.zh: 必须声明被替换对象的路径。
description.en: The path of the object being replaced must be declared.

description.zh: 替换后的对象；缺省 = 取消目标（同 _skip）。
description.en: The replacement object; absent = cancel the target (same as _skip).

description.zh: 声明对象 X 在特定语境中充当对象 Y：X 的物理身份不变，在 scope 内、满足 condition 时其行为等同于 Y（如 <planning_marker> 在支付激活模组费用时视为 <activation_die>），离开语境恢复自身身份。与 <piece>.parts 的静态身份声明互补——parts 表达「载体上印着什么身份」，<substitution> 表达「使用时的身份借用」。domain 为资源、标记等对象概念。
description.en: Declares that object X acts as object Y within a specific context: X's physical identity is unchanged; inside scope, when the condition holds, its behavior equals Y's (e.g. a <planning_marker> counts as an <activation_die> when paying a module's activation cost); outside, it reverts to itself. Complements the static identity declaration of <piece>.parts — parts states which identities are printed on a carrier, <substitution> states an identity borrowed at use time. Domain is object concepts such as resources and markers.

description.zh: 充当的对象——X 被视为什么（如 <activation_die>）。
description.en: The object X is treated as (e.g. <activation_die>).

description.zh: 生效范围的路径式定位——概念.字段.步骤，如 "<activate_module>.<ontology::pipeline>.pay_cost" 表示「activate_module 的 pipeline 中的 pay_cost 步骤」。null = 全场合。
description.en: Path-style scope — concept.field.step, e.g. "<activate_module>.<ontology::pipeline>.pay_cost" = the pay_cost step of activate_module's pipeline. null = everywhere.

description.zh: 适用条件（如「点数与所需一致」）。null = 无条件。
description.en: Applicability condition (e.g. 'value matches the requirement'). null = unconditional.

description.zh: 必须声明充当的对象——X 被视为什么。
description.en: The object being substituted for must be declared.

description.zh: 生效范围。缺省为全场合。
description.en: Scope of effect. Defaults to everywhere.

description.zh: 适用条件。缺省为无条件。
description.en: Applicability condition. Defaults to unconditional.

description.zh: 表示某个 <zone> 或 <object> 归属于哪个 <player> 的 <state>。<ownership> 继承自 <state>。所有权的建立有三种途径：(1) <zone> 推导——<object> 位于 owner 非 null 的 <zone> 中时，该 <zone> 的 owner 隐式拥有该 <object>；(2) 固有归属——<object> 在游戏开始时就已确定属于某 <player>（如玩家自带的牌组），不随 <zone> 变化而改变；(3) 游戏中获取——经由 <transfer>（ownership_change=true）或 <effect> 显式变更所有权。所有权可在游戏过程中被改变——转移、抢夺、赠予或剥夺均须经由规则定义的 <effect> 或 <transfer> 触发。
description.en: A <state> representing which <player> a <zone> or <object> belongs to. <ownership> extends <state>. It is established in three ways: (1) <zone> derivation — when an <object> is in a <zone> whose owner is non-null, that <zone>'s owner implicitly owns the <object>; (2) Intrinsic — the <object> belonged to a <player> from the start of the game, independent of <zone> changes; (3) Acquired — explicitly changed via <transfer> (ownership_change=true) or an <effect> during gameplay. Ownership can change during the game — transferring, stealing, gifting, or revoking must all be triggered by rules-defined <effect>s or <transfer>s.

description.zh: 拥有所有权的 <player>。State 的 subject 字段则指向被拥有的 <zone> 或 <object>。null 表示无所有者（公共区域）。
description.en: The <player> who holds ownership. The State's subject field points to the <zone> or <object> being owned. null = public.

description.zh: 所有权的来源。intrinsic = 游戏开始时即确定（如自备牌组）；zone = 由所在 Zone 的 owner 推导（默认行为）；transfer = 经由 Transfer 或 Effect 在游戏中获得。若未指定，程序默认按 zone 推导。
description.en: The source of ownership. intrinsic = determined at game start (e.g., personal deck); zone = derived from containing Zone's owner (default); transfer = acquired via Transfer or Effect during gameplay. If unspecified, defaults to zone derivation.

description.zh: 标记当前<round>或游戏开始时谁最先行动的<state>。<starting_player>继承自<state>。在多数游戏中，起始玩家由物理的<starting_player_marker>标记——持有<starting_player_marker>的<player>即为起始玩家。每<round>结束后，<starting_player_marker>按规则传递给下一位<player>，<starting_player>随之更新。
description.en: A <state> that marks which <player> acts first in the current <round> or at the start of the game. <starting_player> extends <state>. In most games, the starting player is indicated by a physical <starting_player_marker> — the <player> holding the <starting_player_marker> is the starting player. After each <round>, the <starting_player_marker> is passed to the next <player> according to the rules, and <starting_player> is updated accordingly.

description.zh: 游戏过程中发生的、被游戏规则所识别和定义的、对游戏 <state> 或流程有意义的、不可再分的原子事实。<event> 是流程本体的根概念——一切「发生了什么」都始于 <event>。子类包括 <transfer>、<trigger>、<resolve>、<shuffle>、<play>、<lose>、<gain>。<action> 和 <effect> 均 specifies <trigger>——它们共享 trigger 的完整结构（condition → cost → target → content），仅点火源不同。
description.en: An atomic fact that occurs during gameplay, recognized and defined by game rules, meaningful to game <state> or flow, and not further divisible. <event> is the root of the procedure ontology — everything that "happens" starts from <event>. Subclasses include <transfer>, <trigger>, <resolve>, <shuffle>, <play>, <lose>, <gain>. <action> and <effect> both specify <trigger> — they share trigger's complete structure (condition → cost → target → content), differing only in ignition source.

description.zh: Event 的唯一标识符。用于在规则中精确引用特定事件实例，追溯游戏历史中的因果关系链。
description.en: Unique identifier of the Event. Used to precisely reference a specific event instance and trace causal chains in game history.

description.zh: 导致此事件发生的主体。若事件由玩家主动发起（如 <action>），actor 为该 <player>。若事件由规则自动引发（如 Trigger），actor 为 null。
description.en: The entity that caused this event. If initiated by a player (e.g. <action>), actor is that <player>. If automatically triggered by rules (e.g. Trigger), actor is null.

description.zh: 此事件作用的目标。可以是任意 <object> 的子类实例（<player>、<zone>、<piece> 等）。若事件无特定目标（如「回合开始」），target 为 null。
description.en: The target this event acts upon. Can be any <object> subclass instance (<player>, <zone>, <piece>, etc.). If the event has no specific target (e.g. 'turn begins'), target is null.

description.zh: 此事件的执行规则说明。以中英双语描述事件执行时的具体约束——如「所选宝石颜色必须两两不同」「若不足 3 色则取走全部可用颜色」。这些规则描述超出了结构化字段的表达能力，供 LLM 理解规则和程序实现参考。
description.en: Execution rules for this event. Bilingual description of specific constraints during execution — e.g., 'chosen gems must be of distinct colors', 'if fewer than 3 colors available, take all available'. These rules describe constraints beyond what structured fields capture, serving as reference for LLM understanding and program implementation.

description.zh: 对游戏 <state> 的一个谓词——判断某个命题在当前状态下是否成立，任意时刻可求值、无副作用（只读状态，绝不改变状态）。<condition> 只回答「是」或「否」。谓词的形态不限：位置事实（「此牌在 <development_area> 中」）、历史派生事实（「打出后未超过 3 回合」）、跨玩家比较（「生命值并非全场最高」）、瞬间事实（「回合刚结束」「某 <event> 刚结算完」——只在一瞬为真的 state 事实）均为 <condition>。<condition> 是 Rule Engine 的核心判断单元：<action> 的合法性检查、<trigger> 的激活判断、<endgame_condition> 的触发检测，全部由 <condition> 驱动。<trigger> 对 <condition> 按边沿评估（谓词由假变真的跳变即「进入」，由真变假即「离开」），<continuous_content> 按电平维持（谓词本身）。
description.en: A predicate over the game <state> — evaluates whether a proposition holds under the current state. Evaluable at any moment, side-effect-free (reads state only, never changes it). A <condition> only answers 'yes' or 'no'. Predicates take many forms: location facts ('this card is in the <development_area>'), history-derived facts ('no more than 3 rounds since it was played'), cross-player comparisons ('health is not the highest'), and instantaneous facts ('the turn just ended', 'an <event> just finished resolving' — state facts true only for an instant). <condition> is the core judgment unit of the Rule Engine: <action> legality checks, <trigger> activation, and <endgame_condition> detection are all driven by <condition>s. A <trigger> evaluates its <condition> on the edge (the false→true transition is 'entering', true→false is 'leaving'); a <continuous_content> is maintained on the level (the predicate itself).

description.zh: Condition 的唯一标识符。程序根据此 id 查找对应的 evaluator 函数，传入 params 和当前 GameState，返回 boolean。
description.en: Unique identifier of the Condition. The program looks up the corresponding evaluator function by this id, passes params and current GameState, and returns a boolean.

description.zh: 此条件的参数。内容由具体的条件类型决定。例如 SupplyCount 条件：{ "resource": "blue", "operator": ">=", "value": 4 }。复合条件（AND/OR）：{ "op": "and", "operands": [condition_ref, ...] }。程序根据条件的 id 查找对应的 evaluator 函数，传入 params 和当前 GameState，返回 boolean。
description.en: Parameters for this condition. Content is determined by the specific condition type. E.g., a SupplyCount condition: { "resource": "blue", "operator": ">=", "value": 4 }. Compound conditions (AND/OR): { "op": "and", "operands": [condition_ref, ...] }. The program looks up the evaluator function by the condition's id, passes params and current GameState, and returns a boolean.

description.zh: 时间轴上的一个位置。<timing> 回答「何时发生」，是游戏时间秩序的基础。<timing> 可以是：某个状态变化的瞬间（「任何使宝石总数变化的 <event> 结算完成时」）、阶段边界（「一名 <player> 的回合结束时」）、或某个 <event> 完成后（「此 <action> 执行完毕时」）。<timing> 的持有者有两类：一是 <trigger>——决定何时检查 <condition>，时机到达且条件满足才触发；二是 <procedure>（<round>、<turn>、<phase>）——划定自身的起止边界。普通 <event> 不持有 <timing>——<trigger> 触发后其 <event> 序列按 order 依次执行，顺序本身就是时序，无需逐事件声明。<timing> 本身不改变游戏状态，它只是时间秩序的描述。
description.en: A position on the timeline. <timing> answers 'when does it happen' and is the foundation of the game's temporal order. A <timing> can be: the instant of a state change ('when any <event> that changes the gem total finishes resolving'), a phase boundary ('when a <player>'s turn ends'), or the completion of some <event> ('when this <action> finishes executing'). <timing> has two kinds of holders: <trigger>s — which use it to decide when to check the <condition>, firing only when the timing arrives and the condition holds; and <procedure>s (<round>, <turn>, <phase>) — which use it to delimit their own start and end. Ordinary <event>s do not hold <timing> — once a <trigger> fires, its <event> sequence executes in order, and the sequence itself is the temporality; no per-event declaration is needed. <timing> itself changes no game state — it is merely a description of temporal order.

description.zh: Timing 的唯一标识符。程序根据此 id 查找对应的 watcher 函数，在游戏循环中侦测时机是否到达。
description.en: Unique identifier of the Timing. The program looks up the corresponding watcher function by this id and detects in the game loop whether the timing has arrived.

description.zh: 此时机的参数，内容由具体的时机类型决定。例如事件完成后：{ "after": "<event_id>" }；阶段边界：{ "boundary": "turn_end" }；状态变化瞬间：{ "on_change": { "zone": "<zone_id>", "watch": "count" } }。程序根据时机的 id 查找对应的 watcher 函数，在游戏循环中侦测时机是否到达，返回 boolean。
description.en: Parameters for this timing. Content is determined by the specific timing type. E.g., after an event completes: { "after": "<event_id>" }; a phase boundary: { "boundary": "turn_end" }; the instant of a state change: { "on_change": { "zone": "<zone_id>", "watch": "count" } }. The program looks up the watcher function by the timing's id, detects in the game loop whether the timing has arrived, and returns a boolean.

description.zh: <effect> 或 <trigger> 在结算前必须履行的代价。<cost> 继承自 <property>。代价分两种性质：<instant_cost>——一次性支付，伴随实际资源转移；<continuous_cost>——纯粹的状态检查，不消耗任何东西。二者均缺省即免费。
description.en: The cost that must be fulfilled before an <effect> or <trigger> resolves. <cost> extends <property>. Costs come in two forms: <instant_cost> — a one-time payment involving an actual resource transfer; <continuous_cost> — a pure state check that consumes nothing. When both are absent, the cost is free.

description.zh: 一次性支付的代价，伴随实际的 <event>。
description.en: A one-time cost involving an actual <event>.

description.zh: 纯粹的状态条件，不消耗任何资源。
description.en: A pure state condition that consumes nothing.

description.zh: 一次性支付的代价，伴随实际的 <event>（通常为 <transfer>）。支付完毕即完成，不留持续约束。
description.en: A one-time cost involving an actual <event> (usually a <transfer>). Paid once and done; no ongoing constraint remains.

description.zh: 纯粹的状态条件，不消耗任何资源。在 effect 激活期间持续检查——条件成立方可执行后续 content，条件不成立则阻塞。
description.en: A pure state condition that consumes nothing. Checked continuously while the effect is active — content only executes while the condition holds; blocks otherwise.

description.zh: <resolve> 结算时发生的事。三个独立字段可任意组合。<instant_content>：无条件，一次性执行。<continuous_content>：无条件，电平维持。<effect>：条件触发，分 instant（一次机会）和 continuous（持续武装）两种。
description.en: What happens when <resolve> resolves. Three independent fields, freely combinable. <instant_content>: unconditional, one-shot. <continuous_content>: unconditional, level-maintained. <effect>: conditional, with instant (one chance) and continuous (persistent arming) forms.

description.zh: 无条件，一次性执行完毕。
description.en: Unconditional, executes once and is done.

description.zh: 无条件，激活后电平维持。
description.en: Unconditional, level-maintained after activation.

description.zh: 条件触发。含 <instant_effect> 和 <continuous_effect> 两个独立字段，可任意组合。
description.en: Conditional trigger. Contains two independent fields <instant_effect> and <continuous_effect>, freely combinable.

description.zh: 一种 <trigger>——绑定在 <piece> 上，携带 <condition> 监听状态变化，边沿激活后按 pipeline 结算。<effect> 是 armed 态的 trigger：它被 <resolve> 武装到 <piece> 上，此后由自身的 <condition> 决定何时点火。<effect> specifies <trigger>——不是 trigger 的子类型，而是一次参数填充：effect 填入 trigger 的全部槽位并附加「绑定于 <piece>、由 <condition> 边沿激活」的语义约束。含 <instant_effect>（一次机会）和 <continuous_effect>（持续武装）两个独立字段，可任意组合。与 <action> 互为对偶：action 不依赖 <piece>、由玩家点燃；effect 依赖 <piece>、由状态边沿点燃。
description.en: A <trigger> bound to a <piece>, carrying a <condition> to monitor state changes; upon edge activation, follows the pipeline to settle. <effect> is a trigger in armed form: it is armed onto a <piece> by <resolve>, after which its own <condition> determines when to fire. <effect> specifies <trigger> — not a subtype of trigger, but a parameter binding: effect fills in all of trigger's slots and adds the semantic constraint "bound to a <piece>, edge-activated by <condition>". Contains two independent fields <instant_effect> (one chance) and <continuous_effect> (persistent arming), freely combinable. Counterpart to <action>: action is independent of <piece> and ignited by player; effect depends on <piece> and is ignited by a state edge.

description.zh: 一次机会。condition 满足即执行 cost→content，失败则永远消失。
description.en: One chance. If condition is met, executes cost→content; if it fails, gone forever.

description.zh: 持续武装。每次 condition 满足都执行 cost→content，直到 end_condition 成立、来源离场或被外部移除。end_condition 缺省 = 永不自动终结。
description.en: Persistent arming. Fires cost→content each time condition is met, until end_condition holds, source leaves play, or externally removed. Absent end_condition = never auto-terminates.

description.zh: 一次机会。condition 满足即执行 cost→content，无论成败此 effect 永远消失。用于「打出时」「翻开时」等一次性触发场景。
description.en: One chance. If condition is met, executes cost→content; whether it succeeds or fails, this effect is gone forever. Used for one-shot triggers like 'when played' or 'when revealed'.

description.zh: 持续武装。每次 condition 满足都执行 cost→content，直到 end_condition 成立、来源离场或被外部移除。end_condition 缺省 = 永不自动终结。用于光环、被动能力等持续监听场景。
description.en: Persistent arming. Fires cost→content each time condition is met, until end_condition holds, source leaves play, or externally removed. Absent end_condition = never auto-terminates. Used for auras, passive abilities, and other persistent listening scenarios.

description.zh: 终结条件——成立时此 effect 永久失效。缺省 = 永不自动终结。
description.en: Termination condition — when met, this effect permanently deactivates. Absent = never auto-terminates.

description.zh: 无条件，一次性执行完毕。<resolve> 执行一次，终结。
description.en: Unconditional, one-shot. <resolve> executes once, done.

description.zh: 无条件，激活后电平维持。<resolve> 将其加入生效池，按 <active_condition> 判定适用与否。条件变假自动失效，条件再成立自动恢复。派生值 = 基础值 + Σ 生效池修饰。
description.en: Unconditional, level-maintained after activation. <resolve> adds it to the active pool; applies or lapses based on <active_condition>. Derived value = base + Σ active modifiers. Auto-lapses when condition becomes false; auto-restores when true again.

description.zh: 电平维持谓词。缺省沿用所属 effect 的 condition。
description.en: Level-maintenance predicate. Absent = inherit the owning effect's condition.

description.zh: 决定游戏 <object> 或 <zone> 的信息可以被哪些 <player> 观察，以及这种观察是强制的还是可选的规则。<information_visibility> 继承自 <property>。定义了五种基本状态：Public（公开，必须对所有玩家可见）、Private（私有，仅拥有者可观察且不可公开）、Protected（保护，拥有者可选择是否向其他玩家临时展示）、Partially Public（部分公开，仅部分内容对全员可见）、Hidden（隐藏，所有玩家均不可观察）。可在游戏过程中被 <effect> 改变——一张面朝下的卡被翻转后，其可见性从 Hidden 变为 Public。
description.en: A rule that determines which <player>s can observe the information of a game <object> or <zone>, and whether such observation is mandatory or optional. <information_visibility> extends <property>. It defines five basic states: Public (must be visible to all players), Private (only the owner can observe, cannot be shared), Protected (owner may choose to temporarily reveal to others), Partially Public (only part of the content is visible to all), Hidden (no player can observe). Can be changed during gameplay by <effect>s — a face-down card flipped face-up changes from Hidden to Public.

description.zh: 可见性级别枚举：public = 公开，所有 <player> 均可无条件观察；private = 私有，仅拥有者可观察且不可主动公开；protected = 保护，拥有者可选择是否临时展示；partially_public = 部分公开，集合中仅部分内容对全员可见；hidden = 隐藏，所有 <player> 均不可观察。
description.en: Visibility level enum: public = all <player>s can observe unconditionally; private = only the owner can observe and cannot voluntarily reveal; protected = owner may choose to temporarily reveal; partially_public = only part of the content is visible to all; hidden = no <player> can observe.

description.zh: 游戏流程的执行单元——它定义了「游戏现在处于什么阶段」「接下来该做什么」。<procedure> 的子类（<round>、<turn>、<phase>）语义各异但结构相同：**执行内容优先用 <ontology::pipeline> 定义**（options 序列 + do_after 依赖 + loop 循环），**仅干一件事时可直接持有对应概念（如 <ontology::action>），无需 pipeline 包装**——pipeline 是描述多 trigger/多步骤的工具，不是必包层。<procedure> 自身不再有 children / start / end 字段——步骤顺序与先后依赖由 pipeline 的 do_after 表达，循环边界由 pipeline 的 loop.until 表达，「谁能做某操作」由步骤的 <condition> 表达。嵌套仍是自由形式的：options 里的候选项可以是 <round>、<turn>、<phase> 或普通步骤，一整局游戏本身也可以是一个最外层的 <round>。没有固定的层级，具体嵌套关系由每款游戏的规则决定。
description.en: An execution unit of game flow — it defines 'what stage the game is in' and 'what happens next'. The <procedure> subclasses (<round>, <turn>, <phase>) differ in semantics but share the same structure: **execution content is preferably defined via an <ontology::pipeline>** (options sequence + do_after dependencies + loop), **but a procedure doing a single thing may directly hold the concept itself (e.g. an <ontology::action>) without pipeline wrapping** — a pipeline is a tool for composing multiple triggers/steps, not a mandatory wrapper. <procedure> itself no longer has children / start / end fields — step order and prerequisites come from the pipeline's do_after, loop boundaries from the pipeline's loop.until, and 'who may perform an operation' from a step's <condition>. Nesting remains free-form: candidates in options can be <round>s, <turn>s, <phase>s, or plain steps, and an entire game can itself be an outermost <round>. There is no fixed hierarchy — the nesting is determined by each game's rules.

description.zh: 本 <procedure> 的执行内容（options / type / do_after 结构），仅当执行内容多于一个步骤/行动时使用；单内容时直接持有对应概念（如 <ontology::action>、<ontology::turn>、<ontology::round>）。子类 <round>、<turn>、<phase> 通过它描述多步骤执行：<turn> 用 CHOOSE_ONE 表达多行动选择（执行者轮转是 <turn> 的内建语义）、<phase> 用 options 承载子流程或程序化步骤（setup、结算等）。循环边界不在此字段内——见顶层 loop 字段。
description.en: The execution content of this <procedure> (options / type / do_after structure), used only when the execution content has more than one step/action; a single-content procedure directly holds the concept itself (e.g. an <ontology::action>, <ontology::turn>, or <ontology::round>). The subclasses <round>, <turn>, and <phase> describe multi-step execution through it: <turn> uses CHOOSE_ONE for multi-action selection (turn order is <turn>'s built-in semantics), and <phase> holds child procedures or programmatic steps (setup, resolution, etc.) in its options. Loop boundaries are not part of this field — see the top-level loop field.

description.zh: 本 <procedure> 的循环边界（顶层字段，不属于 <pipeline>）。两种形态：(1) 定次循环 `{ "count": N, "counter": "<名称>" }`——执行内容恰好 N 次（N 为数字或引用，如 "player_count"），counter 可选——循环计数变量（如 era_number），供步骤引用当前迭代号；(2) 条件循环 `{ "until": <condition> }`——重复执行内容直到条件成立（until 为 <condition> 的字符串引用或内联谓词 { zh, en }）。**until 条件在迭代完整执行后检查**——正在进行的迭代（一轮）总是完整跑完才求值：触发条件在轮中被满足时，当前轮照常完成（剩余玩家继续行动），轮末循环才停止。**phase 与 round/turn 正交**：phase（规则上下文）切换不影响 round/turn（执行流程）——上下文切换发生在轮间，「完成当前轮」由 round 的完整性天然保证，无需补完结构。若规则要求触发即中断（罕见），用 round + turn 的「本轮尚未行动」condition 在触发后的阶段补完。<round> 用 count 表达「进行几轮」（口语「进行 4 轮」= count 4；缺省无 loop = 1 次 = 每位玩家恰好一个 turn），用 until 表达「直到条件才结束」（如行动阶段直到阶段标记推到红格）；<phase> 也可持有（如「一直进行到有人达到 15 分」）。缺省 null = 执行一次。
description.en: The loop boundary of this <procedure> (a top-level field, not part of <pipeline>). Two forms: (1) fixed-count loop `{ "count": N, "counter": "<name>" }` — execute the content exactly N times (N is a number or reference such as "player_count"); counter is optional — the loop-count variable (e.g. era_number) referenced by steps for the current iteration; (2) conditional loop `{ "until": <condition> }` — repeat the content until the condition holds (until is a string reference to a <condition> or an inline predicate { zh, en }). **The until condition is evaluated after the iteration completes in full** — an iteration (a round) in progress always finishes before the condition is evaluated: when the trigger condition is satisfied mid-round, the current round completes normally (remaining players keep acting) and the loop stops at the end of the round. **<phase> and <round>/<turn> are orthogonal**: a <phase> (rule context) switch does not interrupt <round>/<turn> (execution flow) — context switches happen between rounds, and 'completing the current round' is guaranteed by the round's completeness, needing no catch-up structure. If a rule truly requires an immediate interruption (rare), use the catch-up pattern: a round whose turn carries a 'has not yet acted this round' condition in the phase after the trigger. <round> uses count for 'how many rounds' ('4 rounds' in colloquial terms = count 4; no loop = 1 pass = exactly one turn per player) and until for 'continue until a condition' (e.g. the action phase until the phase indicator is pushed onto the red space); <phase> may also hold it (e.g. 'keep going until someone reaches 15 points'). Default null = execute once.

description.zh: Procedure 的唯一标识符。用于在规则中精确引用特定流程实例，管理流程间的嵌套和跳转关系。
description.en: Unique identifier of the Procedure. Used to precisely reference a specific procedure instance and manage nesting and transitions.

description.zh: 本 <procedure> 的执行内容定义，见顶层字段声明。多步骤/多行动时持有；单内容时直接持有对应概念（如 <ontology::action>、<ontology::turn>、<ontology::round>）。
description.en: The execution content of this <procedure>; see the top-level field declaration. Held when there are multiple steps/actions; a single-content procedure directly holds the concept itself (e.g. an <ontology::action>, <ontology::turn>, or <ontology::round>).

description.zh: 循环边界（count 定次 / until 条件），见顶层字段声明。缺省 null = 执行一次。
description.en: Loop boundary (count / until); see the top-level field declaration. Default null = execute once.

description.zh: 游戏程序结构中一个完整的、可重复的循环单元。<round> 继承自 <procedure>。**<round> 的内建语义：一次 = 每位 <player> 按座次各行动一轮**（<turn> 按座次轮转推进，从起始玩家开始到末位玩家结束）。**执行次数（口语「进行几轮」）由顶层 loop 字段表达**：次数确定用 `loop.count`（缺省无 loop = 1 次 = 每位玩家恰好一个 turn，「进行 4 轮」= count 4）；次数未知、直到条件才结束用 `loop.until`（如「一直进行到有人达到 15 分」）。一整局游戏本身就是一个最外层的 <round>（「再来一局」=「再来一轮」）。<round> 可直接持有 <phase>、<turn> 或普通步骤（单内容不包 pipeline），多步骤时用 <pipeline> 承载——无需中间的包装层，只有 1 个 <phase> 时省略不写。
description.en: A complete, repeatable cycle in game procedure structure. <round> extends <procedure>. **A round's built-in semantics: one pass = every <player> acts once in seating order** (<turn>s advance by seating order, from the starting player to the last). **The execution count ('how many rounds') is expressed by the top-level loop field**: fixed counts use `loop.count` (no loop = 1 pass = exactly one turn per player; '4 rounds' in colloquial terms = count 4); unknown counts that continue until a condition use `loop.until` (e.g. 'keep going until someone reaches 15 points'). An entire game is itself an outermost <round>. A <round> may directly hold a <phase>, <turn>, or plain step (single content without a pipeline); multi-step content uses a <pipeline> — no intermediate wrapper layers, and a single <phase> may be omitted.

description.zh: 将排他的行动权授予单一 <player> 的执行单元。<turn> 继承自 <procedure>。同一时刻至多一个 <turn> 处于激活状态。行动内容：**持有 <ontology::action>——单候选时直接写概念引用（"<activate_module>"），多候选时该 action 携带 options/type 选择结构（如 {"options": ["<a>", "<b>"], "type": "<ontology::multiple_choice_enum.CHOOSE_ONE>"}）**——「从候选中选一个」是 action 自身的选项字段，不需要 pipeline 包装（options/type 只是 pipeline 的一块构件；整个内容只有一个动作时不叫 pipeline）。每个候选 action 自带 <condition> 决定可用性——不成立 = 该候选不可选（候选级排除），条件互补覆盖时玩家必选其一（「能 A 必须 A，否则跳过」= 跳过作为带「A 不可用」condition 的 action）。多步骤复合动作（非选择、按顺序执行的动作序列）才用 <ontology::pipeline> 承载。执行者（当前玩家）由流程推进按座次顺序轮转决定——轮转是 <turn> 的内建语义，无需字段声明。
description.en: An execution unit that grants exclusive action rights to a single <player>. <turn> extends <procedure>. At most one <turn> is active at any given moment. Action content: **holds an <ontology::action> — a single candidate is a plain concept reference ("<activate_module>"); multiple candidates make the action carry an options/type choice structure (e.g. {"options": ["<a>", "<b>"], "type": "<ontology::multiple_choice_enum.CHOOSE_ONE>"})** — 'picking one from candidates' is the action's own option field, no pipeline wrapper needed (options/type is just one building block of a pipeline; a single action does not warrant being called a pipeline). Each candidate action carries its own <condition> deciding availability — failing = that candidate is not selectable (candidate-level exclusion); with complementary conditions the player must pick one of the available candidates ('if A is possible you must do A, otherwise skip' = skip as an action whose condition is the negation of A's availability). Multi-step compound actions (non-choice sequences executed in order) are carried by an <ontology::pipeline>. The actor (current player) is decided by flow progression in seating order — turn order is <turn>'s built-in semantics and needs no field declaration.

description.zh: 游戏流程中，合法动作集合保持一致、规则上下文不发生强制切换的持续区间。<phase> 继承自 <procedure>。是唯一承载「规则上下文」的 <procedure>——当前 <phase> 决定了哪些 <action> 合法、哪些 <effect> 生效。不强制绑定 <player>，允许完全的自动机阶段（无人阶段，仅有 <trigger> 驱动）。<phase> 的 <ontology::pipeline> options 可以承载 <round>、<turn>、另一个 <phase> 或程序化步骤（setup、结算等）——后者的 pipeline 由流程自动执行而非玩家决策。
description.en: A continuous interval in game flow where the set of legal actions remains consistent and the rule context does not switch. <phase> extends <procedure>. It is the only <procedure> that carries 'rule context' — the current <phase> determines which <action>s are legal and which <effect>s are active. Not required to bind to a <player>, allowing fully automated phases (player-less, driven only by <trigger>s). A <phase>'s <ontology::pipeline> options can carry <round>s, <turn>s, other <phase>s, or programmatic steps (setup, resolution, etc.) — the latter pipelines are auto-executed by the flow rather than player-chosen.

description.zh: <object> 在 <zone> 之间移动或 <ownership> 变更的 <event>。<transfer> 继承自 <event>。
description.en: An <event> where an <object> moves between <zone>s or its <ownership> changes. <transfer> extends <event>.

description.zh: <object> 移出的源 <zone>。必须是游戏中已定义的一个 <zone> 实例。没有 source，转移无从发生。
description.en: The <zone> the <object> moves from. Must be a defined <zone> instance. Without a source, the transfer cannot occur.

description.zh: <object> 移入的目标 <zone>。可以是另一个 <zone>，也可以与 source 相同（如区域内重排序）。也可以是 options/type 结构——从多个候选 <zone> 中选择/全部执行（如 5 条进程轨各放 1 个标记：{"options": [轨...], "type": "<ontology::multiple_choice_enum.EXECUTE_ALL>"}）。
description.en: The destination <zone> the <object> moves to. May differ from source or be the same (e.g., reordering within a <zone>). May also be an options/type structure — choose from or execute across multiple candidate <zone>s (e.g., placing 1 marker on each of 5 progress tracks: {"options": [tracks...], "type": "<ontology::multiple_choice_enum.EXECUTE_ALL>"}).

description.zh: 被移动的 <object>。同时承担 <event> 中 target 的语义——此 <object> 就是该转移事件所作用的目标。两种形式：① 纯引用字符串（如 "<event_card>"）；② 带属性设定的对象——概念 ID 做 key、值为属性设定，转移后对象以该属性状态进入 destination（如 { "<event_card>": { "face": "face_down" } } 表示以背面朝上状态放置）。与 <piece>.parts 的属性写法一致。
description.en: The <object> being moved. Also fulfills the <event> target semantics — this <object> is what the transfer event acts upon. Two forms: ① a plain reference string (e.g. "<event_card>"); ② an object with attribute settings — the concept id as key and the attribute values as its value; the object enters the destination in that attribute state (e.g. { "<event_card>": { "face": "face_down" } } means placed face down). Same attribute syntax as <piece>.parts.

description.zh: 是否同时改变 <ownership>。若为 true，则 destination <zone> 关联的 <player> 成为新所有者。
description.en: Whether <ownership> also changes. If true, the <player> associated with the destination <zone> becomes the new owner.

description.zh: 转移的 <object> 数量。<component>（可互换）可能 > 1；<piece>（不可互换）通常 = 1。
description.en: Quantity of <object>s transferred. <component>s (interchangeable) may be > 1; <piece>s (unique) are usually = 1.

description.zh: 从隐藏集合中抽取 <object> 的抽象概念——抽取前对象不可见，与 <transfer>（移动已知对象）相对。具体抽取规则由子类决定：<top_draw> 从 <deck> 顶部抽（位置规则确定，顶牌未知）；<random_draw> 从 <pool>（袋）中随机抽。游戏层不直接使用本概念。
description.en: The abstract concept of drawing an <object> from a hidden collection — the object is unseen before drawing, as opposed to <transfer> (moving a known object). The concrete drawing rule is determined by the subclass: <top_draw> draws from the top of a <deck> (deterministic position, unseen card); <random_draw> draws blindly at random from a <pool> (bag). Game files do not use this concept directly.

description.zh: 抽取的源 <zone>。必须是隐藏集合——<deck>（牌堆）或 <pool>（袋子）。
description.en: The source <zone> the <object> is drawn from. Must be a hidden collection — a <deck> (stack) or a <pool> (bag).

description.zh: 抽取出的 <object> 移入的目标 <zone>。
description.en: The destination <zone> the drawn <object> moves to.

description.zh: 被抽取的 <object> 类型。抽取前具体是哪个对象未知。
description.en: The type of <object> being drawn. Which specific object is drawn is unknown beforehand.

description.zh: 抽取的 <object> 数量。
description.en: Quantity of <object>s drawn.

description.zh: 从 <deck> 的顶部抽最上面 1 张（或指定数量）——抽取位置规则确定（顶部），但顶牌在抽取前未知。用于翻牌、发牌、暗面抽牌等场景。
description.en: Draw the top 1 card (or a given quantity) from a <deck> — the draw position is deterministic (the top), but the top card is unseen until drawn. Used for revealing cards, dealing, blind draws, etc.

description.zh: 从 <pool>（袋子等）中随机抽 <object>——完全随机，抽取前对象不可见。用于抽袋（芯片、指示物）等场景。
description.en: Draw an <object> at random from a <pool> (bag, etc.) — completely random, the object is unseen before drawing. Used for bag draws (chips, tokens), etc.

description.zh: 一种 <trigger>——由 <player> 的决策直接点燃，不依赖任何 <piece> 即可存在。<action> 与 <trigger> 共享完全相同的结构（<condition> → <cost> → <target> → <content>），区别不在本体层面，而在称呼习惯：规则书和玩家将出现在回合菜单中、由玩家做出、且不依赖 <piece> 的 trigger 称为「行动」。<action> 自身不声明独有字段——所有字段均与 <trigger> 一致。<action> 的 <condition>（若有）用于定义此行动何时可选（菜单可用性），<cost>/<target>/<content> 由玩家在点火时填入。<action> 的 <content> 槽位可以嵌套另一个 <action>、<effect> 或任意 content 形态——正如 <effect> 的 <content> 可以包含 <transfer>，嵌套不改变被嵌套概念自身的类型。判据：不依赖 <piece> + 由 <player> 做出 = action。<action> 与 <effect> 互为对偶：effect 依赖 <piece>、由状态边沿点燃；action 不依赖 <piece>、由玩家决策点燃。
description.en: A <trigger> ignited directly by a <player> decision, existing independently of any <piece>. <action> shares the exact same structure as <trigger> (<condition> → <cost> → <target> → <content>); the distinction lies not in ontology but in naming convention: rulebooks and players call triggers that appear in turn menus, are performed by players, and do not depend on <piece>s, "actions". <action> declares no unique fields of its own — all fields match <trigger>. <action>'s <condition> (if present) defines when this action is available (menu eligibility); <cost>/<target>/<content> are filled by the player at ignition time. <action>'s <content> slot may nest another <action>, <effect>, or any content form — just as <effect>'s <content> may contain a <transfer>, nesting does not change the nested concept's own type. Criterion: independent of <piece> + performed by <player> = action. <action> and <effect> are counterparts: effect depends on a <piece> and is ignited by a state edge; action is independent of any <piece> and is ignited by a player decision.

description.zh: 标记游戏终局流程启动的 <condition>。<endgame_condition> 继承自 <condition>——结构上与普通 <condition> 无异，区别仅在于语义角色：当此 <condition> 评估为 true 时，游戏进入终局流程。终局流程的具体行为由游戏规则定义——可能是立即终止（如「<deck> 被抽空时游戏立刻结束」），也可能先执行一个收尾阶段（如「触发后所有 <player> 补完当前 <round> 再结算」）。典型触发条件：「任意 <player> 达到 10 分」「最后一张 <card> 被抽走」「所有 <tile> 放置完毕」。一局游戏可以有多个 <endgame_condition>——任一满足即触发终局流程。
description.en: A <condition> that marks the start of the endgame process. <endgame_condition> extends <condition> — structurally identical to an ordinary <condition>, differing only in its semantic role: when this <condition> evaluates to true, the game enters its endgame process. What happens during endgame is defined by the specific game's rules — it could be immediate termination (e.g., 'game ends instantly when the <deck> runs out'), or a wrap-up phase first (e.g., 'all <player>s finish the current <round> before final scoring'). Typical trigger conditions: 'any <player> reaches 10 points', 'the last <card> is drawn', 'all <tile>s have been placed'. A game may have multiple <endgame_condition>s — satisfying any one triggers the endgame process.

description.zh: 在终局流程完成后、决定哪位 <player> 胜出的 <condition>。<victory_condition> 继承自 <condition>，其判定标准是一个按优先级排序的 <condition> 序列——按顺序满足条件的 <player>（们）是胜者。判定流程：满足第 1 条 <condition> 的 <player> 为候选胜者；候选多于 1 人时，在候选中继续应用下一条 <condition> 筛选，直到只剩 1 人或序列用完；序列用完仍有多名候选则为平局。与 <endgame_condition> 的分工：<endgame_condition> 回答「游戏何时结束」，<victory_condition> 回答「结束后谁赢」。允许合作胜利（所有 <player> 共同获胜），允许无人获胜（全员失败）。
description.en: A <condition> that determines which <player> wins, evaluated after the endgame process completes. <victory_condition> extends <condition>, and its adjudication standard is an ordered sequence of <condition>s — the <player>(s) satisfying the criteria in order win. Adjudication: <player>s satisfying the 1st <condition> become winner candidates; if more than one remains, apply the next <condition> to the candidates, continuing until exactly one remains or the sequence is exhausted; if multiple candidates remain after the sequence, the result is a tie. Division of labor with <endgame_condition>: <endgame_condition> answers 'when does the game end', <victory_condition> answers 'who wins after it ends'. Cooperative victories (all <player>s win together) are allowed, as is no winner at all (everyone loses).

description.zh: 胜负判定必须给出形式化的条件序列——没有条件序列，程序无法确定胜者。按优先级从高到低排序，每条<condition>都是对单个<player>求值的判定式（如「声望最高」「发展卡最少」）——允许并列，并列者视为同时满足。判定流程：满足第 1 条的<player>为候选；多于 1 人则在候选中应用下一条继续筛选；直到只剩 1 人或序列用完。
description.en: Victory adjudication must provide a formalized condition sequence — without it, the program cannot determine the winner. Sorted from highest to lowest priority; each <condition> is a predicate evaluated per <player> (e.g., 'highest prestige', 'fewest development cards') — ties count as satisfied simultaneously. Adjudication: <player>s satisfying the 1st criterion become candidates; if more than one remains, apply the next criterion to the candidates; continue until exactly one remains or the sequence is exhausted.

description.zh: 可执行规格的最小完整单元：<condition> → <cost> → <target> → <content>，按 pipeline（见 ontology/flow.json）依次结算。<trigger> 是体系的核心机器——所有游戏效果都跑在这同一台机器上。按点火源分为三种角色：(1) 纯 trigger——<condition> 边沿激活，规则自动执行，actor 为 null；(2) <effect>——specifies trigger，绑定在 <piece> 上、由 <condition> 边沿激活；(3) <action>——specifies trigger，不依赖 <piece>、由 <player> 决策点燃。三者共享完全相同的结构（condition/cost/target/content），区别仅在于点火源和称呼习惯。
description.en: The smallest complete unit of executable specification: <condition> → <cost> → <target> → <content>, settled sequentially per the pipeline (see ontology/flow.json). <trigger> is the core machine of the system — all game effects run on this same machine. Three roles by ignition source: (1) pure trigger — <condition> edge-activates, rules auto-execute, actor is null; (2) <effect> — specifies trigger, bound to a <piece>, edge-activated by <condition>; (3) <action> — specifies trigger, independent of any <piece>, ignited by a <player> decision. All three share the exact same structure (condition/cost/target/content), differing only in ignition source and naming convention.

description.zh: 本 trigger 的标准执行流程。缺省引用 ontology/flow.json 的 <trigger_pipeline>：evaluate_condition（不成立终止）→ pay_cost（足额支付，无法足额终止）→ select_target → resolve_content。步骤 id 全局可寻址——其他声明可用路径引用具体步骤（如 substitution 的 scope 写 "<activate_module>.<ontology::pipeline>.pay_cost" 表示「支付费用那一步」）。
description.en: The standard execution flow of this trigger. Defaults to <trigger_pipeline> in ontology/flow.json: evaluate_condition (terminate if false) → pay_cost (pay in full; terminate if impossible) → select_target → resolve_content. Step ids are globally addressable — other declarations may reference a specific step via path (e.g. substitution scope "<activate_module>.<ontology::pipeline>.pay_cost" = the cost-payment step).

description.zh: 触发门槛——对 <state> 的谓词，按边沿评估。也是本 trigger 的 <content>（含 pipeline）能被执行的总体条件。
description.en: The firing gate — a predicate over <state>, evaluated on the edge. It is also the overall precondition for the trigger's <content> (including its pipeline) to execute.

description.zh: 满足 condition 后足额支付的代价。缺省为免费。
description.en: The cost paid in full after condition is met. Absent = free.

description.zh: 代价支付后由 <resolve> 结算的内容。含 <instant_content>（一次执行）、<continuous_content>（电平维持）两个终结形态。<instant_content> 内部可以是 <pipeline>（options / type / do_after 步骤序列）——一个 trigger 触发多个事件（先转移再得分、分支选择等）时用 pipeline 表达，步骤可以是任意操作（<transfer>、<state_change>、<push_track> 等）或对其他概念的引用；<continuous_content> 表达光环类电平效果。
description.en: The content settled by <resolve> after cost payment. Two terminal forms: <instant_content> (one-shot) and <continuous_content> (level-hold). <instant_content> may contain a <pipeline> (options / type / do_after step sequence) — used when one trigger causes multiple events (transfer then scoring, branching, etc.); steps can be any operation (<transfer>, <state_change>, <push_track>, etc.) or references to other concepts; <continuous_content> expresses aura-style level effects.

description.zh: 一种 <trigger>——按 condition → cost → content 执行后，产出 <result>（任意类型）。与通常 trigger 不同，<evaluate> 的 <content> 执行完毕后必须返回一个值，供后续 step 的 condition 引用。
description.en: A <trigger> that produces a <result> (any type) after executing condition → cost → content. Unlike a regular trigger, <evaluate>'s <content> must return a value after execution, which can be referenced by subsequent steps' conditions.

description.zh: 求值完成后产出的返回值。类型取决于具体子类——<check> 为 boolean，通用的 <evaluate> 可为任意类型。
description.en: The return value after evaluation completes. The type depends on the subclass — <check> is boolean; generic <evaluate> can be any type.

description.zh: 产出 pass/fail 结果的 <evaluate>。<result> 的类型特化为 boolean——true 表示通过，false 表示未通过。用于恩惠检定、属性检定、狩猎判定等场景。
description.en: An <evaluate> that produces a pass/fail result. <result> is specialized to boolean — true = passed, false = failed. Used for favor checks, attribute checks, hunting checks, etc.

description.zh: pass 或 fail。
description.en: pass or fail.

description.zh: 将 <content> 应用到游戏 <state> 的 <event>。<resolve> 只接触 content 的三种形态：<instant_content>——执行一次，终结；<continuous_content>——进入生效池，电平维持；<effect>——<instant_effect> 武装一次（condition 满足即 cost→content，失败永远消失），<continuous_effect> 持续武装（每次 condition 满足都 cost→content，直到 end_condition 或来源离场）。
description.en: An <event> that applies <content> to the game <state>. <resolve> only touches content's three forms: <instant_content> — execute once, done; <continuous_content> — enter active pool, level-maintained; <effect> — <instant_effect> arms once (condition met → cost→content, fail → gone forever), <continuous_effect> arms persistently (fires on each condition met, until end_condition or source removed).

description.zh: <resolve> 的本质是将 <content> 实例化为真实的 <event> 并应用到游戏状态——没有 <content>，<resolve> 无事可做。此约束要求子类提供一份可结算的 <content>，指明结算时应发生哪些具体事件。
description.en: The essence of <resolve> is instantiating <content> as real <event>s and applying them to game state — without <content>, <resolve> has nothing to do. This constraint requires subclasses to provide a resolvable <content> specifying what concrete events should occur during resolution.

description.zh: 对某个 <zone>（通常为 <deck> 类型 <reserve>）中全部或部分 <object> 的顺序进行随机重排的 <event>。<shuffle> 继承自 <event>。其结果是使 <object> 的排列从当前已知或可推测的顺序变为不可预测的顺序，同时将该 <zone> 的信息状态从 Partially Public 重置为 Hidden。<shuffle> 可由 <player> 作为 <action> 的一部分主动执行（actor 为 <player>），也可由规则通过 <trigger> 自动要求（actor 为 null）——例如「每当 <discard_pile> 被洗入 <deck> 时自动洗混」。
description.en: An <event> that randomly reorders all or some <object>s in a <zone> (typically a <deck>-type <reserve>). <shuffle> extends <event>. Its result is transitioning the object ordering from a known or inferable sequence to an unpredictable one, while resetting the <zone>'s information state from Partially Public to Hidden. <shuffle> may be actively performed by a <player> as part of an <action> (actor is <player>), or automatically required by rules via a <trigger> (actor is null) — e.g., 'shuffle automatically whenever the <discard_pile> is merged into the <deck>'.

description.zh: 一种用于存放游戏组件的存储型 <zone>。<reserve> 继承自 <zone>，abstract。核心语义是「存放备用」——游戏物件在此被汇集、叠放或陈列，作为游戏物资的库存。物件在 <reserve> 中处于「备用」状态，直到被抽取、购买或以其他方式移入使用中。典型的 <reserve> 子类包括：<supply>（直接取用的可计数存储池；<ownership> 为 null 时是公共供应堆，指向特定 <player> 时是玩家供应堆）、<market>（待获取 <piece> 的陈列区）、<deck>（按序抽取的叠放区）、<pool>（随机化组件的存储区）。
description.en: A storage-type <zone> for holding game components. <reserve> extends <zone>, abstract. Core semantic is 'keeping in storage' — game objects are pooled, stacked, or displayed here as the game's material inventory. Objects in a <reserve> are in a 'reserve' state until drawn, purchased, or otherwise moved into active use. Typical <reserve> subclasses: <supply> (countable direct-take storage pool; public when <ownership> is null, player-specific when <ownership> points to a <player>), <market> (display area of acquirable <piece>s), <deck> (ordered draw stack), <pool> (storage zone for randomizable components).

description.zh: 存放已使用、已消耗或主动弃置的游戏物件的 <zone>。<discard_pile> 继承自 <zone>。物件离开活跃使用状态后进入弃牌堆——卡牌被使用后弃入、<component> 被消耗后归入、<piece> 被摧毁后置入。通常是面朝上的（全员可见），内容物成为所有玩家的公共信息。在许多游戏中可被重新洗入 <deck> 以实现物件的循环复用。在仅有一叠共用卡牌且使用后即弃入的游戏中，弃牌堆就是 <deck> 的「反面」——一个空了，另一个满到可以洗回来。
description.en: A <zone> that holds game components that have been used, consumed, or voluntarily discarded. <discard_pile> extends <zone>. Objects enter after leaving active use — cards played and resolved, <component>s consumed, <piece>s destroyed. Typically face-up (visible to all), making its contents public information. In many games it can be reshuffled back into the <deck> to recycle components. In games with a single shared deck, the <discard_pile> is the <deck>'s 'mirror' — when one empties, the other is full enough to shuffle back.

description.zh: 归属于特定 <player> 的 <zone>，用于存放该玩家个人的游戏组件。<player_zone> 继承自 <zone>，abstract。是 <reserve> 的对偶概念——<reserve> 存放共享的游戏物资，<player_zone> 存放属于单个玩家的东西。owner 始终指向一个 <player> 实例（不可为 null）。典型的子类包括：<player_holding>（玩家手持或暂存的 <piece>）、<development_area>（玩家已打出/建造、正处于活跃使用中的 <piece> 所在区域）。
description.en: A <zone> that belongs to a specific <player>, holding that player's personal game components. <player_zone> extends <zone>, abstract. It is the counterpart to <reserve> — while <reserve> stores shared game materials, <player_zone> stores what belongs to an individual player. owner is always a <player> reference (never null). Typical subclasses: <player_holding> (where a player keeps <piece>s in hand or temporarily), <development_area> (where a player's played/built <piece>s reside in active use).

description.zh: 一种 <piece>，通常为扁平矩形，有正面和背面两个面。<card> 继承自 <piece>。正面承载该卡牌的全部身份信息——名称、费用（<cost>）、效果文本（<effect>）、插画等；背面通常与同 <deck> 中其他卡牌一致，用于隐藏正面信息。卡牌是桌游中最常见的 <piece> 形态，也是 <play> 的主要对象——玩家从手牌（<player_holding> 的子类）中打出卡牌，支付其 <cost>，触发其 <effect>。
description.en: A type of <piece>, typically flat and rectangular, with a front face and a back face. <card> extends <piece>. The front face carries the card's full identity — name, <cost>, <effect> text, illustration, etc.; the back face is usually identical across all cards in a <deck>, serving to conceal the front. Cards are the most common <piece> form in board games and the primary target of <play> — players play cards from their hand (a subclass of <player_holding>), pay their <cost>, and trigger their <effect>.

description.zh: 卡牌的朝向。face_up = 正面朝上（内容可见）；face_down = 背面朝上（内容隐藏）。null 表示不区分正反。
description.en: Which side of the card is showing. face_up = front visible; face_down = back visible. null means the card does not distinguish sides.

description.zh: 一种 <piece>，通常较 <card> 更小更厚，形状不定——六边形、正方形、长方形或不规则形状均有。<tile> 继承自 <piece>。典型例子包括卡坦岛的六角地形板块、卡卡颂的地图板块、Azul 的装饰砖块、多米诺骨牌式拼接板块。
description.en: A type of <piece>, typically smaller and thicker than a <card>, with variable shapes — hexagonal, square, rectangular, or irregular. <tile> extends <piece>. Typical examples: Catan hexagonal terrain tiles, Carcassonne map tiles, Azul decorative tiles, domino-style placement tiles.

description.zh: 板块的朝向。face_up = 正面朝上（内容可见）；face_down = 背面朝上（内容隐藏）。null 表示不区分正反。
description.en: Which side of the tile is showing. face_up = front visible; face_down = back visible. null means the tile does not distinguish sides.

description.zh: 一种 3D 的 <piece>，不同于平面的 <card> 或 <tile>。<token> 继承自 <piece>。典型如工放游戏中的工人、米宝、建筑模型——玩家直接拿起来放下去，不握在手里也不拼在版图上。<token> 可以携带 <effect>、可以被 <play>、可以拥有自己的 <zone>。
description.en: A 3D <piece>, distinct from flat <card>s or <tile>s. <token> extends <piece>. Typical examples include workers in worker placement games, meeples, and building models — the player picks them up and places them directly, without holding them in hand or assembling them on the board. A <token> can carry <effect>s, be <play>ed, and host its own <zone>s.

description.zh: 存放无差别的、可直接取用的 <object> 的 <reserve>。<supply> 继承自 <reserve>。核心语义是「备用且直接取用」——此区域中的 <object> 完全相同且可互相替代（通常为 <component> 或 <resource>），获取方式为直接取用而不需抽取或随机：玩家只决定「取多少」，不决定「取哪个」。对象数量可能有限或无限，不支持顺序操作和洗混。访问权限由 <ownership> 决定：<ownership> 为 null 时是公共供应堆，所有玩家均可取用；<ownership> 为特定 <player> 时是玩家供应堆，仅该玩家可取用。典型例子：璀璨宝石的宝石供应堆、卡坦岛的资源卡供应堆、某些游戏中每位玩家面前分出的资源池。
description.en: A <reserve> that holds undifferentiated <object>s which can be directly taken. <supply> extends <reserve>. Core semantic is 'kept in storage and directly taken' — objects here are identical and interchangeable (typically <component>s or <resource>s), accessed by direct taking without drawing or randomness: the player only decides 'how many', not 'which one'. Quantity may be limited or unlimited; no ordering or shuffling. Access rights are determined by <ownership>: when <ownership> is null it is a public supply open to all players; when <ownership> is a specific <player> it is a player supply accessible only to that player. Typical examples: Splendor's gem supply, Catan's resource card supply, per-player resource pools dealt from a common supply in some games.

description.zh: 存放可见的、各不相同的 <object>，供 <player> 主动选择获取的 <reserve>。<market> 继承自 <reserve>。与 <supply> 的对偶概念——<supply> 存放无差别物件（<player> 只管「取多少」），<market> 存放各不相同物件（<player> 需要决定「取哪个」）。核心特征：(1) 物件各不相同——通常为 <piece>（如 <card>、<tile>），每件有独立的身份和 <property>；(2) 完全可见——所有物件面朝上陈列，成为所有 <player> 的公共信息；(3) 主动选择——<player> 从陈列的物件中指定具体哪一件来获取，而非无差别取用；(4) 获取通常伴随 <cost>——玩家支付对应费用后获得所选物件。典型例子：璀璨宝石的中央卡牌陈列区、四季物语的公共骰子区、 dominion 的王国卡牌供应区。
description.en: A <reserve> that holds visible, distinct <object>s from which <player>s can actively choose and acquire. <market> extends <reserve>. The counterpart to <supply> — while <supply> holds undifferentiated items (player only decides 'how many'), <market> holds distinct items (player must decide 'which one'). Core traits: (1) items are distinct — typically <piece>s (e.g., <card>, <tile>), each with its own identity and <property>; (2) fully visible — all items are displayed face-up as public information for all <player>s; (3) active choice — <player>s designate a specific item to acquire rather than taking undifferentiated units; (4) acquisition usually involves a <cost> — the player pays the associated cost to obtain the chosen item. Typical examples: Splendor's central card display, Seasons' public dice pool, Dominion's Kingdom card supply.

description.zh: 存放有序叠放的 <object> 序列、从固定位置（通常为顶部）抽取的 <reserve>。<deck> 继承自 <reserve>。与 <supply> 和 <market> 不同——<supply> 无序取用、<market> 主动挑选，<deck> 则是从固定的抽取位置按序获取，玩家无法选择取哪一张。核心特征：(1) 有序序列——<object> 之间有严格的先后顺序；(2) 固定抽取位——每次从同一位置（顶部）取走最上方的一张；(3) 支持洗混——<shuffle> 可随机重排整个 <deck> 的顺序，是 <deck> 特有的操作；(4) 默认隐藏——面朝下放置，<information_visibility> 通常为 hidden，洗混后信息状态重置为不可预测。典型例子：Uno 的抽牌堆、璀璨宝石的贵族卡牌堆、卡坦岛的发展卡牌堆。
description.en: A <reserve> that holds an ordered stack of <object>s, drawn from a fixed position (typically the top). <deck> extends <reserve>. Unlike <supply> (undifferentiated taking) and <market> (active choice), a <deck> is drawn from sequentially at a fixed position — the player cannot choose which one to take. Core traits: (1) ordered sequence — <object>s have a strict sequential order; (2) fixed draw position — the topmost <object> is always taken; (3) supports <shuffle> — randomly reordering is a <deck>-specific operation; (4) hidden by default — face-down, <information_visibility> is typically hidden, reset to unpredictable after <shuffle>. Typical examples: Uno's draw pile, Splendor's noble tile deck, Catan's development card deck.

description.zh: 存放各不相同的 <object>、通过随机方式抽取的无序 <reserve>。<pool> 继承自 <reserve>。与 <deck> 的关键区别：<deck> 有固定顺序、从顶部按序抽取、支持 <shuffle>；<pool> 无序、每次抽取为独立随机事件、不支持 <shuffle>——你把手伸进袋子里摸一个，摸到什么是独立概率，不依赖之前的抽取。核心特征：(1) 无序集合——<object> 之间没有先后关系；(2) 随机抽取——每次获取哪一个由随机决定，非玩家选择（区别于 <market>），也非按序获取（区别于 <deck>）；(3) 身份后验——<object> 被抽出后其身份才公开；(4) 概率可调——向 <pool> 中添加或移除特定 <object> 可改变后续抽取的概率分布。典型例子：Scrabble 的字母袋、卡卡颂的板块抽袋、Orléans 的随从抽袋。
description.en: An unordered <reserve> holding distinct <object>s, accessed by random draw. <pool> extends <reserve>. Key difference from <deck>: a <deck> has a fixed order, draws from the top sequentially, and supports <shuffle>; a <pool> is unordered, each draw is an independent random event, and <shuffle> is not supported — you reach into a bag and pull one out; what you get is an independent probability, not dependent on previous draws. Core traits: (1) unordered collection — no sequence among <object>s; (2) random draw — which one you get is determined randomly, not by player choice (unlike <market>) nor by sequence (unlike <deck>); (3) identity post-hoc — the <object>'s identity is only revealed after drawing; (4) adjustable probability — adding or removing specific <object>s changes the probability distribution of subsequent draws. Typical examples: Scrabble's letter bag, Carcassonne's tile bag, Orléans' follower bag.

description.zh: 存放当前未进入游戏流程的 <object> 的 <reserve>。<game_box> 继承自 <reserve>。与 <supply>、<market>、<deck>、<pool> 不同——这些游戏中的 <reserve> 内容直接参与当前游戏状态和规则判定；而 <game_box> 中的 <object> 暂时游离于当前游戏流程之外，既不可被 <player> 取用，也不触发任何游戏规则。核心特征：(1) 初始容器——游戏设置前，所有组件通常先放在 <game_box> 中；(2) setup 阶段入口——游戏设置时从这里取出组件，放入合适的游戏内 <reserve>；(3) 流程外暂存——游戏过程中，某些规则可能要求将 <object> 移回 <game_box>，表示该 <object> 暂时从当前游戏流程中移除（区别于 <discard_pile> 的永久弃置）；(4) 不直接参与规则——<game_box> 中的 <object> 不计入胜负、不可被选择或操作，直到再次进入某个游戏内 <reserve>。典型例子：璀璨宝石盒中尚未分发的发展卡和贵族板块、某些游戏中被规则临时移出流程的卡牌或指示物。
description.en: A <reserve> holding <object>s that are not currently part of the game flow. <game_box> extends <reserve>. Unlike <supply>, <market>, <deck>, and <pool> — in-game <reserve>s whose contents directly participate in the current game state and rules — <object>s in <game_box> are temporarily outside the current game flow: they cannot be taken by <player>s and trigger no game rules. Core traits: (1) initial container — before setup, all components usually start here; (2) setup entry point — during setup, components are taken from here and placed into appropriate in-game <reserve>s; (3) out-of-flow holding — during gameplay, certain rules may move <object>s back into <game_box>, indicating they are temporarily removed from the current game flow (distinct from permanent discarding to <discard_pile>); (4) non-participatory — <object>s in <game_box> do not count toward victory, cannot be selected or operated, until they re-enter an in-game <reserve>. Typical examples: undistributed development cards and noble tiles in the Splendor box, or cards/tokens temporarily removed from play by certain game rules.

description.zh: 归属于单个 <player> 的私有 <player_zone>，用于存放该 <player> 已获得但尚未激活的 <piece> 或 <component>。<player_holding> 继承自 <player_zone>。其核心语义是「保留但未投入使用」——此区域中的 <object> 已经归该玩家所有，但尚未触发 <effect>，不直接参与公共游戏逻辑（如计分、战斗、生产）。<player> 通常可从 <player_holding> 中打出 <piece> 以将其移入公开区域。常见用途：手牌、已保留的卡牌、秘密任务指示物、未建造的板块、个人目标标记、仓库中的资源/材料。注意：因为其中的物件已经属于玩家，所以它不同于 <supply>（供应堆中的物件——无论 <ownership> 是公共还是玩家专属——通常尚未属于玩家）。
description.en: A private <player_zone> belonging to a single <player>, holding <piece>s or <component>s that the <player> has acquired but not yet activated. <player_holding> extends <player_zone>. Its core semantic is 'reserved but not yet in play' — <object>s here already belong to the player but have not had their <effect>s triggered and do not directly participate in public game logic (e.g., scoring, combat, production). The <player> can typically <play> <piece>s from their <player_holding> to move them into a public zone. Common uses: hand cards, reserved cards, secret mission tokens, unbuilt tiles, personal objective markers, resources/materials in storage. Note: because its contents are already owned by the player, it is distinct from <supply> (whose contents — whether public or player-exclusive — are typically not yet owned).

description.zh: 归属于单个 <player> 的公开 <player_zone>，用于放置该 <player> 已打出、已购买或已建造的 <piece>。<development_area> 继承自 <player_zone>。与 <player_holding> 构成对偶——<player_holding> 是「手里攥着还没用的」，<development_area> 是「已经摆出来正在生效的」。核心特征：(1) 公开可见——<information_visibility> 通常为 public，成为所有 <player> 判断对手实力的主要依据；(2) 效果激活——此区域中的 <piece> 的 <effect> 已经或正在持续生效，直接参与公共游戏逻辑；(3) 通常不可逆——<piece> 一旦进入此区域，通常无法退回 <player_holding>，除非规则明确允许。典型例子：万智牌中的战场、璀璨宝石中已购买的卡牌列、卡卡颂中已放置的地图板块。
description.en: A public <player_zone> belonging to a single <player>, holding <piece>s that the <player> has played, purchased, or built. <development_area> extends <player_zone>. The counterpart to <player_holding> — <player_holding> is 'what you're holding but haven't used yet', <development_area> is 'what you've already deployed and is now taking effect'. Core traits: (1) publicly visible — <information_visibility> is typically public, making this the main basis for opponents to assess your strength; (2) effects active — <piece>s here have their <effect>s already or continuously active, directly participating in public game logic; (3) typically irreversible — once a <piece> enters this zone, it usually cannot be returned to <player_holding> unless explicitly allowed by rules. Typical examples: the battlefield in Magic: The Gathering, the purchased card row in Splendor, placed map tiles in Carcassonne.

description.zh: 多步骤操作中的中间态 <zone>，不在任何玩家的常规区域中，也不在规则书中被命名。任何 <object> 均可短暂进入临时区——抽牌检视、暂存待分配的资源、中间计算结果等。临时区中的 <object> 在操作完成前不参与任何游戏判定。操作完成后临时区必须清空——所有 <object> 要么进入目标 zone，要么返回来源 zone。
description.en: An intermediate <zone> used during multi-step operations, not belonging to any player's regular area and not named in the rulebook. Any <object> can briefly enter the temporary zone — cards drawn for inspection, resources awaiting distribution, intermediate computation results, etc. <object>s in the temporary zone do not participate in any game decisions until the operation completes. The temporary zone MUST be empty after the operation — all <object>s either enter their target zone or return to their source zone.

description.zh: 临时区可容纳的最大 object 数量。由于临时区是瞬时使用的，通常无需设上限——null 表示无上限。
description.en: Maximum number of objects the temporary zone can hold. Since the zone is used transiently, typically uncapped — null means unlimited.

description.zh: 所有玩家共用的 <board>，承载公共游戏状态。<public_board> 继承自 <board>。它上面可以容纳公共 <zone>（如轨、展示区）、放置公共 <piece> 和 <component>，并可能携带自身的 <content>。<zone> 的存在和属性由游戏规则独立定义，<public_board> 是它们的物理宿主。物理形态不固定，可由多块板拼接而成；拼接而成的公共版图通过 <components> 列出其组成部分。
description.en: A <board> shared by all players, carrying public game state. <public_board> extends <board>. It can host public <zone>s (e.g., tracks, display areas), hold public <piece>s and <component>s, and may carry its own <content>. <zone>s exist and are defined independently by game rules; the <public_board> is their physical host. Physical form is not fixed and may consist of multiple assembled boards; an assembled public board lists its parts via <components>.

description.zh: 当此公共版图由多块板拼接而成时，列出组成它的 <board> 或 <aid> 实例。单块公共版图可省略此字段。注意：此处只应包含 board 和纯参考 aid，不包含 <piece>、<tile> 等游戏零件——后者属于游戏状态，应放在 <zone> 中。
description.en: When this public board is physically assembled from multiple boards, list the <board> or <aid> instances that compose it. Omit for a single-piece board. Note: only boards and pure reference aids should be listed here; <piece>s, <tile>s, and other game components belong to game state and should reside in <zone>s.

description.zh: 分配给单个 <player> 的专属 <board>，承载该玩家的个人游戏状态。<player_board> 继承自 <board>。它上面可以容纳该玩家专属的 <player_zone>（如模组区、仓库区、收入区等），并可能携带自身的 <content>（如面板上印着的基础活动图标）。通常每个 <player> 各持一块。与 <public_board> 的区别：<public_board> 全员共用，<player_board> 每人一块。
description.en: A personal <board> assigned to a single <player>, carrying that player's individual game state. <player_board> extends <board>. It can host that player's personal <player_zone>s (e.g., module area, storage area, income area) and may carry its own <content> (e.g., the basic activity icon printed on it). Typically each <player> has one. Difference from <public_board>: <public_board> is shared by all, while <player_board> is one per player.

description.zh: 记录规则摘要、流程参考或计分信息的便携 <aid>。<player_aid> 继承自 <aid>。通常为卡片或薄板形式，内容为游戏规则的浓缩或索引——如回合流程速查、所有 <action> 的图标说明、计分规则摘要。可有正反两面。
description.en: A portable <aid> recording rule summaries, procedure references, or scoring information. <player_aid> extends <aid>. Typically a card or thin board containing condensed or indexed game rules — e.g., turn flow quick-reference, icon guide for all <action>s, scoring rule summary. May have two sides.

description.zh: 完整记录游戏规则、流程和组件说明的文档型 <aid>。<rulebook> 继承自 <aid>。通常在游戏开始前阅读学习，游戏中可作为参考查阅。不参与游戏逻辑的运作——即使没有 <rulebook>，游戏规则依然存在并生效。<rulebook> 只是规则的书面载体，不是规则本身。
description.en: A document-type <aid> that fully records the game's rules, procedures, and component descriptions. <rulebook> extends <aid>.
