Typically read before the game starts and used as a reference during play. Does not participate in game logic — even without the <rulebook>, the game rules still exist and apply. The <rulebook> is merely the written carrier of rules, not the rules themselves.

description.zh: 游戏的虚构世界观、时代背景与关键角色设定，用于解释风味名称、主题和叙事元素，不直接参与规则判定。<setting> 继承自 <object>。例如，在《文明演化》中，玩家是创世技术学院的学生，正在参加名为「文明演化」的考试；考试场地是一片僻静的大陆，每位考生都必须成为当地的一名神祇，发展并引领自己的文明，在与其他文明的竞争中取得成功，胜者将晋升为创世技术学院的正式成员。阿格拉（Agera）是这场考试的主考官，因此代表考生获得其青睐程度的轨被称为 <favor_of_ager_track>（阿格拉恩惠轨）。
description.en: The fictional world view, historical backdrop, and key character setup of a game, used to explain flavor names, themes, and narrative elements without directly participating in rule adjudication. <setting> extends <object>. For example, in Civolution, players are students of the Genesis Tech Academy taking an exam called 'Civilization Evolution'. The exam takes place on a remote continent; each candidate must become a local deity, develop and lead their own civilization, and outcompete the others. The winner becomes a full member of the Genesis Tech Academy. Agera is the examiner of this exam, so the track that records how much favor each candidate has earned is called the <favor_of_ager_track> (Favor of Agera track).

description.zh: 一种有序的 <zone>，用于放置 <marker> 并记录某个数值或进度的当前状态。<track> 继承自 <zone>。与普通 zone 的区别在于：object 在 track 中通常只做内部位置移动（前进/后退），不发生 zone 之间的 transfer。典型例子包括计分轨、进程轨、天气轨、阶段序列、恩惠轨等。
description.en: An ordered <zone> used to place <marker>s and record the current value or progress of some numeric or ordinal state. <track> extends <zone>. Unlike a regular zone, objects in a track usually only move internally (forward/backward) rather than being transferred between zones. Typical examples include score tracks, progress tracks, weather gauges, phase sequences, and favor tracks.

description.zh: 此轨的槽位定义，必填。**parts 形式**（与 <piece>.parts 同款）：数组元素声明「格段」——每个元素是一个 part，概念 ID 做 key，值为属性对象（或纯概念引用字符串 = 1 格）：`{ "<reset_space>": { "count": 9 } }`。属性：count（格数，默认 1）、scope（可选——数值轨的数值范围，如 "1–100"）、parts（可选——本 part 内部再分多个子 part，如行动阶段段 = [黄格 part（重置推格）, 红格 part（重置不推，触发轮+下一轮结束自动推）]）、description（可选）。数字轨写一个 part + count（格数）与 scope（数值范围）；槽位轨每类格一个 part（语义相同的多格共用一个 part + count）。**引用格式**：单格 part（count 1）直接写 `<track>.<part_id>`（如 "<phase_sequence>.<phase_2_new_goals>"）；多格 part 写 `<track>.<part_id>[n]`——n 为 part 内 0 基偏移（如 "<phase_sequence>.<phase_4_action>[9]" = 行动阶段段第 10 格；description 中用「第 n+1 个」对照表述，避免偏移误导）。marker 的当前位置即其所在格——以「<marker> 位于 <track>.<part_id>」或「<marker> 位于 <track>.<part_id>[n]」表达。
description.en: Slot definitions for this track, required. **Parts form** (same style as <piece>.parts): array elements declare 'space segments' — each element is a part whose key is a concept id with an attribute object as value (or a plain concept-reference string = 1 space): `{ "<reset_space>": { "count": 9 } }`. Attributes: count (number of spaces, default 1), scope (optional — the numeric range of a numeric track, e.g. "1–100"), parts (optional — sub-parts within this part, e.g. an action-phase segment = [yellow-space part (Reset advances), red-space part (Reset does not advance; auto-advances after the triggering round + next round)]), description (optional). Numeric tracks use one part with count (spaces) and scope (range); slot-based tracks use one part per class of space (semantically identical multiple spaces share one part + count). **Reference format**: single-space parts (count 1) are referenced directly as `<track>.<part_id>` (e.g. "<phase_sequence>.<phase_2_new_goals>"); multi-space parts use `<track>.<part_id>[n]` with n the 0-based offset within the part (e.g. "<phase_sequence>.<phase_4_action>[9]" = the 10th space of the action-phase segment; descriptions phrase it as 'the n+1-th space' to avoid offset confusion). A marker's current position is its containing space — expressed as "<marker> is on <track>.<part_id>" or "<marker> is on <track>.<part_id>[n]".

description.zh: 用于记录 <player> 的 <score> 数量的 <track>。<score_track> 继承自 <track>。通常是公共版图的一部分或外框，每位玩家各用一个 <marker> 在此轨上指示自己当前拥有多少 <score>。<score> 本身是 <resource>，「玩家有 N 分」才是 <state>；分轨是这个 <state> 的可视化载体。
description.en: A <track> used to record how much <score> each <player> has. <score_track> extends <track>. It is usually part of or the outer frame of the public board; each <player> uses a <marker> on this track to indicate how many <score> they currently have. <score> itself is a <resource>; 'Player has N points' is the <state>. The score track is the visual carrier of this <state>.

description.zh: 存放 <card> 的 <player_holding>，是最常见的玩家保留区形态。<hand> 继承自 <player_holding>。<information_visibility> 通常为 private（仅拥有者可观察）或 protected（拥有者可选择向其他 <player> 展示），但具体可见性由游戏规则决定。<hand> 是 <play> 的主要源区域——<player> 从手牌中打出 <card>，将其移入 <development_area> 或 <discard_pile>。
description.en: A <player_holding> that holds <card>s, the most common form of player holding. <hand> extends <player_holding>. <information_visibility> is typically private (only the owner can observe) or protected (owner may choose to reveal to other <player>s), but the specific visibility is determined by game rules. <hand> is the primary source zone for <play> — a <player> plays a <card> from their hand, moving it to the <development_area> or <discard_pile>.

description.zh: 一种特化的 <action>：<player> 的选择内容是从可用的 <effect> 池中激活某一个。<activation> specifies <action>——填入 action 的全部槽位并将 target 窄化为「选哪个 <effect>」。<player> 选择一个可用的 <effect> 并将其激活，该 <effect> 随即从静默（dormant）进入待结算（pending）状态，等待后续的 <resolve> 将其 <content> 应用到游戏 <state>。<activation> 不等同于 <resolve>——激活后效果可能排队等待，多个同时激活的 <effect> 需要通过优先级决定结算顺序。候选 <effect> 可能来自 <piece>（如研究牌上的活动能力）、<board>（如控制台自带的基础活动）、或其他游戏组件。
description.en: A specialized <action>: the <player>'s choice is to activate one <effect> from a pool of available effects. <activation> specifies <action> — fills in all of action's slots and narrows target to "which <effect>". The <player> selects an available <effect> and activates it, transitioning it from dormant to pending state to await subsequent <resolve> which applies its <content> to the game <state>. <activation> is not the same as <resolve> — after activation, effects may queue; multiple simultaneously activated <effect>s require priority ordering for resolution. Candidate <effect>s may come from <piece>s (e.g., activity abilities on research cards), <board>s (e.g., the innate activity on a console), or other game components.

description.zh: 被激活的 <effect>。<activation> 的本质是使一个 <effect> 从静默转入待结算——没有 <effect>，激活无事可做。此约束要求子类指明从可用 <effect> 池中选择了哪一个。
description.en: The <effect> being activated. The essence of <activation> is transitioning an <effect> from dormant to pending — without an <effect>, activation has nothing to do. This constraint requires subclasses to specify which <effect> was chosen from the available pool.

description.zh: 用于产生随机数值的游戏组件。<dice> 继承自 <object>。每颗骰子有若干面，每面印有一个数值或符号；通过 <die_roll> 事件掷出后，根据朝上的一面确定结果。骰子本身没有 <effect>，不可被 <play>，只是随机数生成器。
description.en: A game component used to generate random values. <dice> extends <object>. Each die has several faces, each printed with a value or symbol; after being rolled via a <die_roll> event, the result is determined by the face that lands upward. Dice themselves have no <effect> and cannot be <play>ed — they are random number generators.

description.zh: 骰子的面数。如六面骰为 6。
description.en: Number of faces on the die. E.g., 6 for a six-sided die.

description.zh: 骰子当前朝上的面所显示的点数。用于结构化表达对骰子点数的要求——如 cost 中要求的特定点数、或 content 中产生的随机结果。null 表示尚未掷出或无需指定。
description.en: The value shown on the currently upward face of the die. Used to structurally express die value requirements — e.g., a specific value required in a cost, or a random result produced in content. null means not yet rolled or not specified.

description.zh: 满足其中任意一个即可的费用形式。多个替代条件之间是 OR 关系。
description.en: A cost form where satisfying any one of the listed conditions is sufficient. Multiple alternatives are OR-related.

description.zh: 替代费用选项列表。
description.en: List of alternative cost options.

description.zh: 玩家在执行 <action> 或 <effect> 时必须做出的多选决策。
description.en: A multi-option decision a player must make when executing an <action> or <effect>.

description.zh: 可选项列表。
description.en: List of available options.

description.zh: 投掷一颗或多颗 <dice> 以产生随机数值的 <event>。<die_roll> 继承自 <event>。结果由骰子朝上的一面决定，可用于判定、费用、资源获取等。玩家通常可以花费创意标记等资源修改骰子点数。
description.en: An <event> in which one or more <dice> are rolled to generate random values. <die_roll> extends <event>. The result is determined by the face(s) that land upward and can be used for checks, costs, resource gains, etc. Players may often spend resources such as idea markers to modify die results.

description.zh: <object> 失去一个 <property>。失去后该 property 的 domain 变为 null。常用于 effect 的载体切换——当 effect 不再由某个实体持有时，该实体 lose 此 effect。
description.en: An <object> loses a <property>. The property's domain becomes null after losing. Commonly used when an effect's carrier changes — when an effect is no longer held by an entity, that entity loses this effect.

description.zh: 失去属性的实体。必须指明是哪个 <object> 在失去属性。
description.en: The entity losing the property. Must specify which <object> is losing the property.

description.zh: 被失去的属性。必须指明失去的是哪个 <property>（或 <effect>）。
description.en: The property being lost. Must specify which <property> (or <effect>) is being lost.

description.zh: <object> 获得一个 <property>。获得后该 property 的 domain 指向此 object。常用于 effect 的载体切换——当 effect 改由新的实体持有时，新实体 gain 此 effect。
description.en: An <object> gains a <property>. The property's domain points to this object after gaining. Commonly used when an effect's carrier changes — when an effect becomes held by a new entity, that entity gains this effect.

description.zh: 获得属性的实体。必须指明是哪个 <object> 在获得属性。
description.en: The entity gaining the property. Must specify which <object> is gaining the property.

description.zh: 被获得的属性。必须指明获得的是哪个 <property>（或 <effect>）。
description.en: The property being gained. Must specify which <property> (or <effect>) is being gained.

description.zh: 一个 <object> 的某个属性的值从 A 变为 B。与 <lose>/<gain> 不同——后者操作的是 <property> 的 domain 归属；<state_change> 操作的是 <state> 的属性值（如部落的站立→躺倒、卡牌的横置→竖置、token 的正面→反面）。
description.en: The value of an <object>'s attribute changes from A to B. Distinct from <lose>/<gain> — those operate on <property> domain ownership; <state_change> operates on <state> attribute values (e.g., tribe standing→lying, card tapped→untapped, token face-up→face-down).

description.zh: 状态发生变更的 <object>。
description.en: The <object> whose state is changing.

description.zh: 变更后的目标状态值，用点号路径表达。
description.en: The target state value after the change, expressed as a dot-path.

description.zh: 变更的属性名。多数情况下状态自身即语义——如 <strong> 不需要套在 'posture' 下。仅当同一个 object 有多个正交状态维度时才需要（如一张卡同时有 'orientation' 和 'face' 两个状态）。
description.en: The attribute name being changed. Usually unnecessary — states carry their own semantics (e.g., <strong> doesn't need a 'posture' wrapper). Only needed when an object has multiple orthogonal state dimensions (e.g., a card with both 'orientation' and 'face' states).

description.zh: 变更前的旧 <state>。可不写——表示无论当前是什么状态，强制设为目标状态。
description.en: The old <state> before the change. Optional — if absent, unconditionally set to the target state.

description.zh: 将 <card> 或 <tile> 翻至另一面。attribute 固定为 face，to 为 face_up 或 face_down。
description.en: Flip a <card> or <tile> to its other side. Attribute is fixed to face; to is face_up or face_down.

description.zh: 一个 <state_change>：object 的 level 属性从 A 变为 B。subject 为被升级的 object，attribute 固定为 level，to 为目标等级。level 提升可能伴随载体切换——当新旧 level 由不同实体承载时，旧载体 <lose> 旧 effect、新载体 <gain> 新 effect；当同一载体承载（如 tile 翻面）时，仅为 level 变化，无 lose/gain。物理操作（翻面、移除板块）是 level 变化的物理后果，由游戏层表达。
description.en: A <state_change>: an object's level attribute changes from A to B. subject is the object being upgraded, attribute is fixed to level, to is the target level. Level increase may involve carrier switch — when old and new levels are carried by different entities, the old carrier <lose>s the old effect and the new carrier <gain>s the new effect; when carried by the same entity (e.g., tile flip), it is purely a level change with no lose/gain. Physical operations (flip, remove tile) are consequences of the level change, expressed at the game layer.

description.zh: 将一个 <piece> 投入使用的 <event>。依次：支付 <piece>.<effect>.<cost>、将 <piece> <transfer> 到目标 <zone>、<resolve> <piece>.<effect>.<content>。
description.en: An <event> that puts a <piece> into use. Sequentially: pay <piece>.<effect>.<cost>, <transfer> the <piece> to the destination <zone>, <resolve> <piece>.<effect>.<content>.

description.zh: 被打出的 <piece>。
description.en: The <piece> being played.

description.zh: <piece> 的来源 <zone>。
description.en: The source <zone> of the <piece>.

description.zh: <piece> 移入的目标 <zone>。
description.en: The destination <zone> for the <piece>.

description.zh: 打出流程的执行步骤配置。包含 pay_cost（支付费用）、transfer_piece（转移 piece）、resolve（结算内容）三个步骤，按 do_after 声明依赖顺序依次执行。
description.en: Execution step configuration for the play procedure. Contains three steps — pay_cost, transfer_piece, resolve — executed in dependency order declared by do_after.

description.zh: 执行策略，固定为 EXECUTE_ALL——全部步骤按依赖顺序执行。
description.en: Execution strategy, fixed to EXECUTE_ALL — all steps execute in dependency order.

description.zh: 将一条 <track> 上的标记向前推进。桌游中最通用的位移 <event> 之一——计分、进程、天气等所有轨道共享此语义。两种形态：(1) `step`——推进几格；(2) `to`——推进到目标格（槽位轨的 slot 引用，如 "<phase_sequence>.phase_5"，需要轨的 slots 定义了每格 id）。
description.en: Advance a marker on a <track>. One of the most universal displacement <event>s in board games — shared semantics across score tracks, progress tracks, weather gauges, etc. Two forms: (1) `step` — advance by a number of spaces; (2) `to` — advance to a target space (a slot reference on a slot-based track, e.g. "<phase_sequence>.phase_5"; requires the track's slots to define per-space ids).

description.zh: 要推进的轨道。类型在子类中窄化为具体轨道。
description.en: The track to advance on. Narrowed to a specific track in subclasses.

description.zh: 往前推进几个格。与 to 二选一。
description.en: Number of steps to advance. Mutually exclusive with to.

description.zh: 推进到的目标格——槽位轨 slot 的路径引用（"<track>.<slot_id>"，如 "<phase_sequence>.phase_5"）。与 step 二选一。
description.en: The target space to advance to — a path reference to a slot on a slot-based track ("<track>.<slot_id>", e.g. "<phase_sequence>.phase_5"). Mutually exclusive with step.

description.zh:
多选项的处理模型。从几个 token 中选一个拿走，从几个 action 中选一个执行，一个流程有好几个步骤按什么顺序进行——这些都是「从多个候选中做出选择并执行」的问题。<pipeline> 用 <options> 数组承载候选项，用 <type> 引用 <multiple_choice_enum> 决定处理策略，用 <do_after> 表达依赖。候选项可以是任何东西——<ontology::transfer>、<ontology::action>、另一个 <pipeline>、甚至是 <null>（表示「什么都不做」也是一种合法选择）。当一个流程涉及多种不同类型的子操作、难以用单个 extends/specifies 归类时使用。

**<pipeline> 是唯一的结构原语——<round>、<turn>、<phase> 用 <pipeline> 定义多步骤实际流程**（children 数组、actor、start/end 字段均已废弃：流程顺序由 options + do_after 表达，循环由 <procedure> 顶层的 loop 字段表达，「谁能做」由步骤的 <condition> 表达，行动权轮转是 <turn> 的内建语义）。单内容时 procedure 直接持有对应概念（如 <ontology::action>、<ontology::turn>、<ontology::round>），不包 pipeline。<pipeline> 也是通用可挂载结构——任何概念都可以选择持有它：<trigger>（<action>/<effect>）把它作为多事件执行内容放在 <content>.<instant_content> 内（或直接持有）；<cost> 可用于多步支付的复杂代价；<content> 可用于多步骤的效果结算。持有是可选的、由使用方按需书写，不为此给每个概念设计专属字段——和 <options> 字段一样的通用模式。
description.en:
A model for handling multiple options. Picking one token from several, choosing one action to perform, deciding the order of steps in a procedure — these are all the same problem: selecting and executing among multiple candidates. A <pipeline> uses the <options> array for candidates, <type> to reference <multiple_choice_enum> for the selection strategy, and <do_after> for dependencies. Candidates can be anything — a <ontology::transfer>, an <ontology::action>, another <pipeline>, or even <null> (doing nothing is a valid choice). Use when a procedure involves sub-operations of different types that are hard to classify under a single extends/specifies.

**<pipeline> is the single structural primitive — <round>, <turn>, and <phase> define their multi-step actual flow with a <pipeline>** (the children array, actor, and start/end fields are all deprecated: ordering comes from options + do_after, repetition from the <procedure>-level loop field, 'who may act' from a step's <condition>, and turn order is <turn>'s built-in semantics). A single-content procedure directly holds the concept itself (e.g. an <ontology::action>, <ontology::turn>, or <ontology::round>) without a pipeline. <pipeline> is also a universal mountable structure — any concept may choose to hold it: <trigger> (<action>/<effect>) places it inside <content>.<instant_content> (or holds it directly) as multi-event execution content; <cost> may use it for complex multi-step payments; <content> may use it for multi-step resolution. Holding is optional and written by the user as needed — no per-concept dedicated fields are designed, following the same universal pattern as the <options> field.

description.zh: 候选项数组。里面装什么由具体场景决定——可以是 <ontology::card>、<ontology::tile>、<ontology::resource>（从几个组件中选一个拿走），也可以是 <ontology::transfer>、<ontology::action>、子 pipeline（从几个操作中选一个执行），也可以是 <ontology::player>、<ontology::zone>（从几个目标中选一个作用）。null 表示「什么都不做」——被选中时跳过执行，但在 do_after 链上视为已完成。**候选级 condition 语义**：候选项携带的 <condition> 决定其可用性——condition 不成立 = 该候选项不可选（从选择池排除），不影响其他候选；与步骤级阻断（options 顶层项的 condition 不成立 = 该步骤及其 do_after 依赖项全部停止）相区分。「如果 A 可用则必须 A，否则 B」的表达：B 作为带「A 不可用」condition 的候选（如「跳过」的 condition 是全部行动条件取反），使候选 condition 互补覆盖所有情况，CHOOSE_ONE 从可用候选中必选其一。
description.en: Array of candidates. What goes inside is determined by the specific scenario — it could be <ontology::card>s, <ontology::tile>s, <ontology::resource>s (picking a component to take), <ontology::transfer>s, <ontology::action>s, sub-pipelines (choosing an operation to perform), or <ontology::player>s, <ontology::zone>s (picking a target to affect). null means 'do nothing' — when selected, execution is skipped but the do_after chain treats it as completed. **Candidate-level condition semantics**: a candidate's <condition> decides its availability — a failing condition excludes that candidate from the pool without affecting the others; this differs from step-level blocking (a top-level option whose condition fails stops that step and everything depending on it via do_after). To express 'if A is available you must do A, otherwise B', give B a candidate condition that is the negation of A's availability (e.g. a 'skip' candidate whose condition is the AND of all action conditions being false), so candidate conditions cover all cases complementarily and CHOOSE_ONE picks exactly one from the available candidates.

description.zh: 处理策略，引用 <multiple_choice_enum>——EXECUTE_ALL：按依赖顺序全部执行（拓扑排序）；CHOOSE_ONE：从中选一个；CHOOSE_AT_LEAST_ONE：至少选一个；CHOOSE_ANY：任意组合（每项最多一次）。
description.en: Selection strategy, referencing <multiple_choice_enum> — EXECUTE_ALL: execute all in dependency order (topological sort); CHOOSE_ONE: pick exactly one; CHOOSE_AT_LEAST_ONE: pick at least one; CHOOSE_ANY: any subset, each at most once.

description.zh: 前置依赖。仅当 do_after 中的所有项都完成（或跳过）后才可执行本项。每个候选项内部也可有自己的 do_after。
description.en: Prerequisite dependencies. This item only becomes executable after all entries in do_after are completed (or skipped). Each candidate may also have its own do_after.

description.zh: 多选项的选择方式枚举，适用于 <effect>、<cost>、<content> 的 options 字段。
description.en: Enum for multi-option selection, used by the options field of <effect>, <cost>, and <content>.

description.zh: 枚举值：EXECUTE_ALL = 全部执行，CHOOSE_ONE = 选择 1 个执行，CHOOSE_AT_LEAST_ONE = 选择至少 1 个执行，CHOOSE_ANY = 任意数量执行（0 到全部，每项最多 1 次）。
description.en: Enum values: EXECUTE_ALL = execute all, CHOOSE_ONE = choose one, CHOOSE_AT_LEAST_ONE = choose at least one, CHOOSE_ANY = choose any (0 to all, each at most once).
